Among these: that which is unpleasant at both beginning and end is <s>picumandapāka</s> (neem-ripening); that which is unpleasant at first but moderate in the end is <s>badarapāka</s> (jujube-ripening); unpleasant at first but pleasant in the end is <s>mṛdvīkāpāka</s> (grape-ripening); moderate at first but unpleasant at the end is <s>vārttākapāka</s> (eggplant-ripening); moderate at both beginning and end is <s>tintiḍīkapāka</s> (tamarind-ripening); moderate at first but pleasant at the end is <s>sahakārapāka</s> (mango-ripening); excellent at first but unpleasant at the end is <s>kramukapāka</s> (areca-ripening); excellent at first but moderate at the end is <s>trapusapāka</s> (cucumber-ripening); and pleasant at both beginning and end is <s>nālikerapāka</s> (coconut-ripening). Among these, in each of the first three groups, the first three types of maturity should be rejected. Better to be a non-poet than a bad poet. For bad poetry is a death accompanied by sighs. The middling ones should be refined. For refinement enhances the quality of everything. Even twelve-carat gold becomes pure gold through the ripening of fire. The rest should be accepted. For that which is naturally pure does not require refinement. A grinding stone does not have the power to enhance the brilliance of a pearl.

children.translated_text: Here itself, the threefold method has been shown for disciples;
but this variety also exists in the three worlds.

body.text: iti rājaśekharakṛtau kāvyamīmāṃsāyāṃ kavirahasye prathame 'dhikaraṇe vyutpattikavipākānāṃ nirupaṇaṃ pañcamo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth chapter, entitled 'The Examination of Erudition and Poetic Maturity,' in the first section of the <s>Kavirahsya</s> (Secrets of the Poet) in the <s>Kāvyamīmāṃsā</s> composed by <s>Rājaśekhara</s>.
Chapter 6

body.text: padavākyavivekaḥ
body.translated_text: The Discrimination of Words and Sentences (<s>padavākyaviveka</s>)

body.text: ṣaṣṭho 'dhyāyaḥ 6
body.translated_text: Sixth chapter, section 6.

body.text:
padavākyavivekaḥ vyākaraṇasmṛtinirṇītaḥ śabdo niruktanighaṇṭvādibhirnirdiṣṭastadabhidheyo 'rthastau padam /
tasya pañca vṛttayaḥ subvṛttiḥ, samāsavṛttiḥ, taddhitavṛttiḥ, kṛdvṛttiḥ, tiṅvṛttiśca /
gauraśvaḥ puruṣo hastīti jātivācinaḥ śabdāḥ /
haro harirharaṇyagarbhaḥ kāla ākāśaṃ digiti dravyavācinaḥ /
śvetaḥ kṛṣṇo raktaḥ pīta iti ca guṇavācinuḥ /
pācakaḥ pāṭhaka iti kriyāvācinaḥ prādayaścādayaśvāsattvavacanāḥ /
nagaramupa prasthitaḥ panthāḥ, vṛkṣamanu dyotate vidyuditi karmapravacanīyāḥ /
"seyaṃ subvṛttiḥ pañcatayyapi vāṅmayasya mātā"iti vidvāṃsaḥ /
subvṛttireva samāsavṛttiḥ /
vyāsasamāsāvesānayorbhedahetū /
sā ca ṣoḍhā dvandādibhedena /

children.translated_text: On this, the verse praising compounds (<s>samāsa-sūkta</s>) —

children.text: "dvando 'smi dvigurasmi ca gṛhe ca me satatamavyayībhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: "I am a <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound), I am a <s>dvigu</s> (numeral compound), and in my house there is always <s>avyayībhāva</s> (indeclinable compound);

children.text: tatpuruṣa karma dhāraya yenāṅgaṃ syāṃ bahuvrīhiḥ" //
children.translated_text: <s>tatpuruṣa</s> (determinative compound) is my work, cherish me — may I have <s>bahuvrīhi</s> (possessive compound) as a limb."

body.translated_text: The distinction between word and sentence: A word (<s>pada</s>) is a sound determined by grammar and <s>smṛti</s>, designated by <s>nirukta</s> (etymology), <s>nighaṇṭu</s> (glossaries), etc., together with its denoted meaning. It has five formations (<s>vṛtti</s>): the <s>sub-vṛtti</s> (simple word-form), the <s>samāsa-vṛtti</s> (compound formation), the <s>taddhita-vṛtti</s> (secondary derivative formation), the <s>kṛd-vṛtti</s> (primary derivative formation), and the <s>tiṅ-vṛtti</s> (verbal conjugation). Words denoting genus (<s>jāti</s>): cow, horse, man, elephant. Words denoting substance (<s>dravya</s>): <s>Hara</s>, <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, time, space, direction. Words denoting quality (<s>guṇa</s>): white, black, red, yellow. Words denoting action (<s>kriyā</s>): cook, reader. And the particles <s>pra</s> etc. and <s>ca</s> etc. express existence. <s>Karmapravacanīya</s> (case-governing particles): "the road leading toward the city," "lightning flashes along the tree." "This <s>sub-vṛtti</s>, even in its fivefold form, is the mother of all speech" — thus say the learned. The <s>samāsa-vṛtti</s> (compound formation) is itself the <s>sub-vṛtti</s> [in compound form]. <s>Vyāsa</s> (analytic) and <s>samāsa</s> (synthetic) are the two causes of distinction between them. And it is sixfold, by the division into <s>dvandva</s> etc.

body.text:
tadvitavṛttiḥ punaranantā /
taddhi śāstraprāyovādo yadutataddhitamūḍhāḥ pāṇinīyāḥ /
māñjiṣṭaṃ raucanikaṃ sauraṃ saindhavaṃ vaiyāsīyamiti vaddhitāntāḥ /
prātipadikaviṣayā ceyam /
kṛdvṛttiśca dhātuviṣayā /
karttā harttā kumbhakāro nagarakāra iti kṛdantāḥ /
tiṅvṛttirdaśadhā daśalakārībhedena /
dvidhā ca sā dhātusubdhātuviṣayatvena /
apākṣīt pacati pakṣyatīti dhātavīyānyākhyātāni /
apallavayat pallavayati pallavayiṣyatīti saubdhātavīyāni /
tadidamitthaṅkāraṃ pañcaprakāramapi padajātaṃ mithaḥ samantrīyamānamānantyāya kalpate /
tajjanmā caiṣa viduṣāṃ vādo yatkila divyaṃ samāsahasraṃ bṛhaspatirvaktā śatakraturadhyetā tathāpi nāntaḥ śabdarāśerāsīt /
tatra dayitasubvṛttayo vidarbhāḥ /
vallabhasamāsavṛttayo gauḍāḥ /
priyataddhitā dākṣiṇātyāḥ /
kṛtprayogarucaya udīcyāḥ /
abhīṣṭatiṅgavṛttayaḥ sarve 'pi santaḥ /
teṣāṃ ca viśeṣalakṣaṇānusandhānenāvarddhatākhyātagaṇaḥ /

children.translated_text: And it has been said —
"The usages that shine forth for those who know the special characteristics —
by these, this mass of verbal forms is augmented day by day."

body.translated_text: The <s>taddhita-vṛtti</s> (secondary derivative formation), moreover, is infinite. For it is said that the science [of grammar] is predominantly about <s>taddhita</s> — those <s>Pāṇinīyas</s> (grammarians) who are bewildered by <s>taddhita</s>. <s>Māñjiṣṭha</s> (madder-colored), <s>raucanika</s> (related to orpiment), <s>saura</s> (solar), <s>saindhava</s> (from Sindh), <s>vaiyāsīya</s> (pertaining to <s>Vyāsa</s>) — these are <s>taddhita</s>-ending words. And this pertains to the <s>prātipadika</s> (nominal stem) domain. The <s>kṛd-vṛtti</s> pertains to the verbal root domain. Maker, bearer, potter, city-builder — these are <s>kṛt</s>-ending words. The <s>tiṅ-vṛtti</s> is tenfold, by the division into ten <s>lakāras</s> (tense-mood markers). And it is twofold, by pertaining to primary roots and secondary (denominative) roots. "He cooked," "he cooks," "he will cook" — these are primary verbal forms. "He made sprout," "he makes sprout," "he will make sprout" — these are denominative verbal forms. This entire class of words, of five kinds thus constituted, when mutually combined, tends toward infinity. And this is the origin of the debate among the learned — that the divine <s>Bṛhaspati</s> was the speaker and <s>Śatakratu</s> (<s>Indra</s>) the student of a hundred thousand [words in grammar], yet there was no end to the mass of words. In this regard: the <s>Vaidarbhas</s> are fond of the <s>sub-vṛtti</s>; the <s>Gauḍas</s> are fond of the <s>samāsa-vṛtti</s> (compound formation); the <s>Dākṣiṇātyas</s> (Southerners) are fond of <s>taddhita</s>; the <s>Udīcyas</s> (Northerners) delight in the use of <s>kṛt</s>; and all good people are fond of the <s>tiṅ-vṛtti</s> (verbal conjugation). And through the investigation of their special characteristics, the class of verbal forms has increased.

body.text:
padānāmabhidhitsitārthagranthanākaraḥ sandarbho vākyam /
"tasya ca tridhābhidhāvyāpāraḥ" ityaudbhaṭāḥ /
vaibhaktaḥ śāktaḥ śaktivibhaktimayaśca /
pratipadaṃ śrūyamāṇāsūpapadavibhaktiṣu kārakavibhaktiṣu vā vaibhaktaḥ /
lutpāsvapi vibhaktiṣu samāsasāmarthyāttadarthāvagatau śāktaḥ /
ubhayātmā ca śaktivibhaktimayaḥ /

children.translated_text: An example of the inflectional type —
"Homage to that <s>Varāha</s> (Boar) who playfully lifts up the Earth,
between whose hooves <s>Meru</s> crumbles with a crunching sound."

body.translated_text: A sentence (<s>vākya</s>) is a composition (<s>sandarbha</s>), the repository of the stringing together of words for their intended meaning. "And its expressive function is threefold" — say the followers of <s>Udbhaṭa</s>: inflectional (<s>vaibhakta</s>), power-based (<s>śākta</s>), and a combination of power and inflection (<s>śaktivibhaktimaya</s>). When the case-endings — whether co-occurring case-endings (<s>upapadavibhakti</s>) or case-endings denoting syntactic relations (<s>kārakavibhakti</s>) — are heard with each word, that is the inflectional type. When the meaning is grasped through the power of compounding even when the case-endings are elided, that is the power-based type. And that which partakes of both is the combined type.

children.translated_text: The power-based type —
"With enemies terrified, the people full of longing, feudatories surrendered, of lofty spirit,
endowed with the quality of magnanimity, with the earth conquered by the sword — there is no king other than you."
Or as follows —
"With garlands of deep-blue <s>indīvara</s> (blue lotus) swaying at the neck,
as if sheltering the entire clan of <s>Kāliya</s> serpents out of fear of <s>Hari</s>."
The combined type (power and inflection) —
"Then one day there came, with the radiance on his face illuminating all four directions,
the autumn season, like <s>Brahmā</s>, seated on a fully blossoming lotus."
In this regard, a sentence is tenfold:

children.text: ekākhyātam, anekākhyātam, āvṛttākhyātam, ekābhidheyākhyātaṃ, pariṇatākhyātam, anuvṛttākhyātaṃ, samucutākhyātam, adhyāhṛtākhyātaṃ, kṛdabhihitākhyātam, anapekṣitākhyātamiti //
children.translated_text: with a single verb, with multiple verbs, with a repeated verb, with verbs having one object, with a transformed verb, with a continuing verb, with a fitting verb, with a supplied verb, with a verb expressed through a <s>kṛt</s> (participle), and with an independent verb.
An example of a single verb —
"Victorious is he who with one foot has conquered all three worlds,
whose <s>tāṇḍava</s> (cosmic dance) is bewildered in the placement of the second foot — <s>Śiva</s>!"

body.text:
anekākhyātam-
tacca dvidhā sāntaraṃ nirantaram //
body.translated_text: Multiple verbs — and this is twofold: with intervals and without intervals.

children.translated_text: The first of these —

children.text: "devāsurāstamatha manthagirāṃ virāme padmāsanaṃ jaya jayeti babhāṣire ca /
children.translated_text: "When the churning-mountain ceased [to turn], the gods and demons praised <s>Padmāsana</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) with cries of 'Victory! Victory!";

children.text: prāgbhejire ca parito bahu menire ca ṭa svāgresaraṃ vidadhire ca vavandire ca" //
children.translated_text: and they approached from all sides, greatly honored him, considered him foremost, made him their leader, and bowed down."
The second —

children.text: "tvaṃ pāsi haṃsi tanuṣe manuṣe bibharṣi vibhrājase sṛjasi saṃharase virauṣi /
children.translated_text: "You protect, you destroy, you expand, you create humans, you bear, you shine forth, you create, you annihilate, you roar,

children.text: āḥse nirasyasi sarasyasi rāsi lāsi saṅkrīḍase bruḍasi meghasi modase ca" //
children.translated_text: you pervade, you cast away, you play in lakes, you give, you play, you sport, you speak, you thunder, you rejoice."

body.text:
"ākhyātaparatantraghā vākyavṛttirato yāvadākhyātamiha vākyāni" ityācāryāḥ /
"ekākāratayā kārakagrāmasyaikārthatayā ca vacovṛtterekamevedaṃ vākyam" iti yāyāvarīyaḥ /

children.translated_text: Repeated verb —
"Victorious is <s>Hari</s> whose shoulder-platform is adorned with a cluster of spotless <s>Kaustubha</s> [gems]; victorious are the doe-eyed women with their shifting sidelong glances;

children.text: tato jayati mallikā tadanu sarvasaṃvedanā-vināśakaraṇakṣamo jayati pañcamasya dhvaniḥ" //
children.translated_text: then victorious is the jasmine, and thereafter victorious is the sound of the fifth [note], capable of destroying all sensation!"

body.translated_text: "The sentence construction depends on verbs — there are as many sentences as there are verbs" — say the teachers. "By the unity of form and by the unity of meaning of the group of syntactic relations (<s>kāraka</s>), this is but a single sentence" — says <s>Yāyāvarīya</s>.

children.translated_text: Single-object verb —

children.text: "hṛṣyati cūteṣu ciraṃ tuṣyati bakuleṣu bhodate maruti /
children.translated_text: "He delights in the mango trees, he rejoices in the <s>bakula</s> trees, he thrills at the wind;

children.text: iha hi madhau kalakūjuṣu pikeṣu ca prīyate rāgī" //
children.translated_text: here indeed in spring, the passionate one takes pleasure in the cuckoos with their sweet cooing."
Transformed verb —
"In this [season] is victorious the elixir of the fifth [note] of the five-arrowed one (<s>Kāma</s>);
and those breezes of <s>Caitra</s> month, sporting among the wondrous <s>lākā</s>, <s>kollī</s>, and <s>keli</s> [flowers]."
Continuing verb —
"Elephants roam in the pleasure-gardens at the shores of the four oceans;
and those qualities of yours, bright as <s>kunda</s> flowers, [roam] in the groves of the <s>Cakravāla</s> mountains."
Fitting verb —
"Burdened by the weight of possessions, driven by the course of misfortune,

children.text: mano gantrīva kupathe cītkaroti ca yāti ca" //
children.translated_text: the mind, like a traveler on a wrong path, both groans and goes on."
And also —

children.text: "sa devaḥ sā daṃṣṭrā kiṭikṛtavilāsasmitasitā dvayaṃ diśyāttubhyaṃ mudamidamudāraṃ jayati ca /
children.translated_text: "That god, that tusk — white with the playfully smiling beauty — may this pair grant you joy; this noble [pair] is victorious!
The earth, with its trembling inhabitants agitated by rising fear — when at its tip, by his breaths, it displayed the sport of a rolling mountain-ball."
Supplied verb (<s>adhyāhṛta</s>) —
"He who bears a fragment of the <s>ḍamaru</s> drum dislodged by the <s>tāṇḍava</s> (dance) of his arms,
whose foot-path is strewn with scattered flower-offerings — may that moon-crested <s>Śiva</s> [bring] prosperity to you!"
Verb expressed through a <s>kṛt</s> (participle) —
"The glance was withdrawn when facing me; the laughter arose on the pretext of another topic;

children.text: vinayavādhitavṛttiratastayā na vivṛto madano na ca saṃvṛtaḥ" //
children.translated_text: her behavior was restrained by modesty — by her, love was neither revealed nor concealed."
Independent verb (<s>anapekṣita</s>) —
"How deep is the water, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>?" "Knee-deep, O King."
"Even so, this is your condition — not everyone, O river-crosser, is like you!"

body.text: guṇavadalaṅkṛtañca vākyameva kāvyam //
body.translated_text: A sentence that is endowed with qualities (<s>guṇa</s>) and adorned with ornaments (<s>alaṃkāra</s>) is itself poetry (<s>kāvya</s>).

body.text: "asatyārthābhidhāyitvānnopadeṣṭavyaṃ kāvyam"ityeke //
body.translated_text: "Because it asserts unreal things, poetry should not be taught" — say some.

children.translated_text: For example —

children.text: "stemaḥ stoko 'pi nāṅge śrasitamavikalaṃ cakṣuṣāṃ saiva vṛttiḥ madhyekṣīrābdhi magnāḥ sphutamatha ca vayaṃ ko 'yamīdṛkprakāraḥ /
children.translated_text: "Not even a little perspiration on the body, the eyes function exactly the same, clearly we are plunged in the midst of a milk-ocean — what manner [of strangeness] is this?

children.text: itthaṃ digbhittirodhakṣatavisaratayā māṃsalaistvadyaśobhiḥ stokāvasthānadusthaistrijagati dhavale vismayante mṛgākṣyaḥ" //
children.translated_text: Thus, because your fame, which is fleshy and white, spreads through all the three worlds, breaking through the walls of the directions, the doe-eyed women are astonished at so little space remaining."
And also —

"With the palate of the netherworld blown by the wind from the hoods of the falling, bent Lord of Serpents, with the ocean made turbulent by the harsh collision with the peaks of the rows of great mountains being shattered,

with the celestial nymphs being freed from the dense, unbroken, tawny [dust] rising from the slaughter of demons — such was the tumult of the army of the world-conquering one, when he set forth for battle."
And they say —

children.text: "dṛṣṭaṃ kiñcidadṛṣṭamanyadaparaṃ vācālavārttārpitaṃ bhūyastuṇḍapurāṇataḥ pariṇataṃ kiñciñca śāstraśrutam /
children.translated_text: "Something has been seen, something else unseen, another thing acquired from gossip and chatter, much has matured from ancient tales, and something has been learned from scripture;

children.text: sūktyā vastu yadatra citraracanaṃ tatkāvyamavyāhataṃ ratnasyeva na tasya janma jaladherno rohaṇādvā gireḥ" //
children.translated_text: that which is poetry here — a wondrous composition of fine sayings — is unobstructed, like a jewel whose birth is neither from the ocean nor from the mountain <s>Rohana</s>."
"No [poetry does not assert unreal things]" — says <s>Yāyāvarīya</s> —
"There is nothing unreal whatsoever in poetry; what is <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory statement) in hymns of praise —

children.text: sa na paraṃ kavikarmaṇi śrutau ca śāstre ca loke ca" //
children.translated_text: that is not paramount in the work of the poet, neither in the <s>śruti</s> (revealed scripture), nor in the <s>śāstra</s> (treatise), nor in the world."
An example from <s>śruti</s> (revealed scripture) —
"His two legs that walk are blossoming; the self is fruitful, bearing fruit;

children.text: śere 'sya sarve pāpmānaḥ śrameṇa prapathe hṛtāḥ" //
children.translated_text: all his sins lie [destroyed], carried away by exertion on the road."
An example from <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) —

children.text: "āpaḥ pavitraṃ prathamaṃ pṛthivyāmapāṃ pavitraṃ paramaṃ ca mantrāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Waters are the first purifier on earth, and <s>mantras</s> are the supreme purifier of waters;

children.text: teṣāṃ ca sāmargyajuṣāṃ pavighatraṃ maharṣayo vyākaraṇaṃ nirāhuḥ" //
children.translated_text: and among those [mantras] — the <s>Sāman</s>, <s>Ṛc</s>, and <s>Yajus</s> — the great sages have declared grammar to be their purifier."
Furthermore —
"He who, being skilled in the specialty [of grammar], employs words correctly at the time of usage,
he attains infinite victory in the hereafter — while one who knows the rules of speech is corrupted by incorrect words."

body.text:
"kaḥ? /
vāgyogavideva /
kuta etat ? /
yohi śabdāñjānātyapaśabdānapyasau jānāti /
yathaiva hi śabdajñāne dharmaḥ, evamapaśabdajñaghānepyadharmaḥ /
athavā bhūyānadharmaḥ prānpoti /
bhūyāṃso hṛpaśabdā alpīyāṃsaḥ śabdāḥ /
ekaikasya hi śabdasya bahavo 'prabhraṃśāḥ /
tadyathā /
gaurityasya śabdasya gāvo goṇī gotā gopātaliketyevamādayo 'pabhraṃśāḥ /
atha yo 'vāgyogavid ajñānaṃ tasya śaraṇam /
viṣama upanyāsaḥ /
nātyantāyājñānaṃ śaraṇaṃ bhavitumarhati /
yo hyajānanvai brāhmaṇaṃ hanyātsurāṃ vā pibetse 'pi manye patitaḥ syāt /
evaṃ tarhi so 'nantamāpnoti jayaṃ paratra vāgyogavidduṣyati cāpaśabdaiḥ /
kaḥ? /
avāgyogavideva /
atha yo vāgyogavid vijñaghānaṃ tasya śaraṇam /
kva punaridaṃ paṭhitam? /
bhrājā nāma ślokāḥ /
kiñca bhoḥ ślokā api pramāṇam? /

children.translated_text: "What of it?"
"If [verses are] a valid authority, then this verse too should be authoritative:"
"If a great circle of pots the color of <s>udumbara</s> (fig-tree),

children.text: pītaṃ na gamayetsvargaṃ kiṃ tatkratugataṃ nayet" //
children.translated_text: when drunk, does not convey one to heaven — would that which is performed in a sacrifice do so?"

body.translated_text: "Who [attains this]? The one skilled in the rules of speech, indeed. How so? Because he who knows correct words also knows incorrect words. For just as there is merit (<s>dharma</s>) in the knowledge of correct words, so too there is demerit (<s>adharma</s>) in the knowledge of incorrect words. Or rather, one incurs greater demerit. For incorrect words are more numerous and correct words fewer. For each correct word has many corruptions. For example: <s>gaur</s> — its corruptions are <s>gāvī</s>, <s>goṇī</s>, <s>gotā</s>, <s>gopātalikā</s>, etc. Now, for one who does not know the rules of speech, ignorance is his refuge." "This is an unfair argument. Ignorance cannot be a refuge in the absolute sense. For one who unknowingly kills a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> or drinks liquor — I think even he would be fallen." "Then [the verse means]: 'He attains infinite victory in the hereafter — while one who knows the rules of speech is corrupted by incorrect words.' Who? The one who does not know the rules of speech, indeed. But for one who knows the rules of speech, knowledge is his refuge." "Where has this been recited?" "In the verses called <s>Bhrājā</s>." "But sir, are verses also a valid authority (<s>pramāṇa</s>)?"

children.translated_text: An example from worldly [speech] —
"By your fame that spreads, mixed with the passion for [your] virtues,
half-<s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron) has suddenly appeared on the faces of the bride-directions."

body.translated_text: "This is a song of a drunkard; the [verse] of the revered one that was sung by one who was not intoxicated — that alone is authoritative" — says <s>Gonardīya</s>.

children.translated_text: For example —

children.text: "vayaṃ bāvye ḍimbhāṃstaruṇimani yūnaḥ pariṇatāv apīcchāmo dṛddhānpariṇayavidhestu sthitiriyam /
children.translated_text: "In childhood we desire boys, in youth young men, in old age

children.text: tvayārabdhaṃ janma kṣapayitumamārgeṇa kimidaṃ na no goghatre putri kvacidapi satīlāñchanamabhūt" //
children.translated_text: even old men — this is the way of marriage rites; you have begun to destroy your life by a wrong path — nowhere in our family, O daughter, has there been the mark of a faithful wife!"

body.translated_text: "Because it teaches improper conduct, poetry should not be taught" — say others.

ya evaṃvidhā vidhayaḥ parastrīṣu puṃsāṃ sambhavanti tānavabudhyeteti kavīnāṃ bhāvaḥ /

children.translated_text: As they say —
"As long as the luminous words made of poetry circulate on earth,
so long does the poet rejoice, having attained the abode of <s>Sarasvatī</s>."

body.translated_text: "This teaching exists, but as something to be prohibited, not as something to be prescribed" — says <s>Yāyāvarīya</s>. The intention of poets is that one should understand those kinds of improper conducts that men engage in with other men's wives [so as to avoid them]. Moreover, worldly conduct depends on the words of poets. "And that [worldly conduct] is the root of the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>)" — say the great sages.

children.translated_text: Furthermore —

children.text: "śrīmanti rājñāṃ caritāni yāni prabhutvalālāśva sudhāśināṃ yāḥ /
children.translated_text: "The glorious deeds of kings, the playful speeches of the gods, the nectar-eaters,

children.text: ye ca prabhāvāstapasāmṛṣīṇāṃ tāḥ satkavibhyaḥ śrutayaḥ prasūtāḥ" //
children.translated_text: and the powers of the austerities of sages — these revelations have been born from excellent poets."
And it has been said —

children.text: "khyātā narādhipatayaḥ kavisaṃśrayeṇa rājāśrayeṇa ca gatāḥ kavayaḥ prasiddhim /

children.text: yasya praṇetā tadihānavadyaṃ sārasvataṃ vartma na kasya vandyam ?" //
children.translated_text: that which was composed by him — that blameless path of <s>Sarasvatī</s> — to whom is it not worthy of reverence?"

children.translated_text: For example:
"Creeping along the necklines, filling the brow-valleys and bellies, clanking and terrible, it proclaims the boldness of young women toward their lovers —
Due to the interchange of amorous movements, the tinkling sound of the beautiful golden girdle, split and bursting forth from the slapping of the hip-surface."

body.translated_text: "Poetry should not be taught because it expresses improper meanings" — thus say some.

children.translated_text: And also:
"May young women always be fond of you — those with varied ornamental leaf-designs, with pale cheek-lines from the stretch of their earrings,
with hip-slopes set dancing by the pangs of desire, delightful with the jingling of jeweled girdles."

yadidaṃ śrutau śāstre copalabhyate /

children.translated_text: Among these, from the <s>Yajurveda</s>:

children.text: "upopa me parāmṛśa mā me dabhrāṇi manyathāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Come close to me, touch me; do not think my [parts] are too few —
I am entirely hairy, like a ewe among the <s>Gāndhāra</s> [sheep]."

body.translated_text: "This subject, though having arisen as erotic, is indeed fit to be composed" — thus says the <s>Yāyāvarīya</s> (follower of Yāyāvara). For this is found in both the <s>Śruti</s> (Veda) and the <s>śāstra</s> (treatise).

children.translated_text: From the <s>śāstra</s> (treatise):
"She whose [bodily part] is clear and white, with eyelashes at its edges,
Soft as fresh butter — that becomes her temple of <s>Smara</s> (Love)."
This is the distinction of word and sentence (<s>padavākyaviveka</s>) — [the chapter] slightly bows [to a close].
Now learn also some other types of sentences.

body.text: iti rājaśekharakṛtau kāvyamīmāṃsāyāṃ kavirahasye prathame 'dhikaraṇe ṣaṣṭho 'dhyāyaḥ padavākyavivekaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus in the work composed by <s>Rājaśekhara</s>, in the <s>Kāvyamīmāṃsā</s>, in the <s>Kavirahasya</s>, in the first section — the sixth chapter, the <s>Padavākyaviveka</s> (Distinction of Word and Sentence), ends.

body.text: vākyavidhayaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Vākyavidhayaḥ</s> (Types of Sentences)

body.text: satpamo 'dhyāyaḥ 7
body.translated_text: Seventh chapter, 7

body.text:
vākyavidhayaḥ, kākuprakārāḥ, pāṭhapratiṣṭhā vākyaṃ vacanamiti vyavaharanti /
tacca tridhā praṇetṛbhedena brāhyaṃ, śaivaṃ, vaiṣṇavamiti /
tadidaṃ vāyuproktapurāṇādibhya upalabdhaṃ yaduta brāhyaṃ vacaḥ pañcadhā svāyambhuvamaiśvaramārṣamārṣīkaputrakaṃ ca /
svayambhūrbrahmā tasya svāyambhuvam /
tanmanojanmāno bhṛguprabhṛtayaḥ putrāste īśvarāsteṣāmaiśvaram /
īśvarāṇāṃ sutā ṛṣayasteṣāmārṣam /
ṛṣīṇāmapatyāni ṛṇīkāsteṣāmārṣīkam /
ṛṣīkāṇāṃ sūnava ṛṣiputrakāsteṣāmārṣiputrakam /
svayambhuvaḥ prathamaṃ vacaḥ śrutiḥ, śruteranyañca svāyambhuvam /

children.translated_text: Thus they say:
"That speech which pertains to the soul of all beings, and which contains reproach,
And is sometimes aimed at the meaning of liberation — that is called <s>Svāyambhuva</s> speech."

body.translated_text: <s>Vākyavidhayaḥ</s> (Types of Sentences), <s>kākuprakārāḥ</s> (types of tonal expression), <s>pāṭhapratiṣṭhā</s> (establishment of recitation). A sentence is conventionally called '<s>vacana</s>' (utterance). And that is threefold according to the distinction of authors: <s>Brāhya</s> (pertaining to <s>Brahmā</s>), <s>Śaiva</s> (pertaining to <s>Śiva</s>), and <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> (pertaining to <s>Viṣṇu</s>). This is understood from the <s>Purāṇas</s> narrated by <s>Vāyu</s> and others — namely, the <s>Brāhya</s> speech is fivefold: <s>Svāyambhuva</s> (of <s>Svayambhū</s>), <s>Aiśvara</s> (of the Lords), <s>Ārṣa</s> (of the Sages), <s>Ārṣīka</s> (of the disciples of sages), and <s>Ārṣiputraka</s> (of the sons of sages). <s>Svayambhū</s> is <s>Brahmā</s> — his [speech] is <s>Svāyambhuva</s>. His mind-born sons are <s>Bhṛgu</s> and others — they are the Lords; theirs is <s>Aiśvara</s>. The sons of the Lords are the sages — theirs is <s>Ārṣa</s>. The offspring of the sages are the <s>Ṛṣīkas</s> (sage-disciples) — theirs is <s>Ārṣīka</s>. The sons of the <s>Ṛṣīkas</s> are the <s>Ṛṣiputrakas</s> (sage-grandsons) — theirs is <s>Ārṣiputraka</s>. The first speech of <s>Svayambhū</s> (Brahmā) is <s>Śruti</s> (Veda); other [speech] from <s>Svayambhū</s> is also <s>Svāyambhuva</s>.

body.text: tadeva stokarupāntarapariṇatamaiśvaraṃ vacaḥ /

children.translated_text: And it is said:
"Clear in sequence, unabridged, brilliant, profound, meaningful,

children.text: pratyakṣaṃ ca parokṣaṃ ca lakṣyatāmaiśvaraṃ vacaḥ" //
children.translated_text: Both direct and indirect — observe [such] <s>Aiśvara</s> speech."

body.translated_text: That same [speech], slightly transformed in form, is <s>Aiśvara</s> speech.

children.translated_text: <s>Ārṣa</s> (of the Sages):
"Whatever is combined with <s>mantras</s>, endowed with noun-inflections,
And whose meaning is directly expressed — that is known as the speech of the sages."
<s>Ārṣīka</s> (of sage-disciples):
"That which [employs] various Vedic words, abounds in particles,
And is not very lengthy — that is the speech of <s>Ṛṣīkas</s>."
<s>Ārṣiputraka</s> (of sage-grandsons):
"That which mostly consists of unclear words, and is full of many doubts,
That would be the speech of sage-sons — full of lamentation."

body.text:
tadudāharaṇāni purāṇebhya upalabheta /
sārasvatāḥ kavayo naḥ pūrve itthaṅkāraṃ kathayanti /
brahmaviṣṇurudraguhabṛhaspatibhārgavādiśiṣyeṣu catuḥṣaṣṭāvupadiṣṭaṃ vacaḥ pārameśvaram /
krameṇa ca sañcaraddevairdevayonibhiśca yathāmatyupajīvyamānaṃ divyamiti vyapadiśyate /

children.translated_text: And the divine beings are:
"<s>Vidyādharas</s>, <s>Apsarases</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>,
<s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Guhyakas</s>, <s>Bhūtas</s>, and <s>Piśācas</s> — [these are] the divine beings."

body.translated_text: Examples of these should be gathered from the <s>Purāṇas</s>. The poets of the <s>Sārasvata</s> tradition, our predecessors, narrate thus. The <s>Pārameśvara</s> (Supreme Lord's) speech, taught to the sixty-four disciples of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Guha</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Bhārgava</s>, and others — and in sequence, passing through gods and divine beings, adopted according to their understanding — is designated as 'divine.'

body.text:
tatra piśācādayaḥ śivānucarāḥ svabhūmau saṃskṛtavādinaḥ, martye tu bhūtabhāṣayā vyavaharanto nibandhanīyāḥ /
atsarasastu prākṛtabhāṣayā /
taddivyaṃ vacaścaturddhā /
vaibudhaṃ vaidyādharaṃ gāndharvaṃ yoginīgataṃ ca /
śeṣāṇāmeteṣvevopalakṣaṇaṃ prakṛtisādṛśyena /

children.translated_text: Among these, <s>Vaibudha</s> (of the gods):
"Compact and expansive, filled with <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) and <s>adbhuta</s> (marvelous) [sentiments],
With alliteration and noble — such is the speech of the nectar-eaters (gods)."

body.translated_text: Among these, the <s>Piśācas</s> and others, attendants of <s>Śiva</s>, speak Sanskrit in their own realm, but in the mortal world they should be composed as speaking in <s>Bhūtabhāṣā</s> (the language of spirits). The <s>Apsarases</s>, however, [speak] in <s>Prākṛta</s>. That divine speech is fourfold: <s>Vaibudha</s> (of the gods), <s>Vaidyādhara</s> (of the <s>Vidyādharas</s>), <s>Gāndharva</s> (of the <s>Gandharvas</s>), and <s>Yoginīgata</s> (of the <s>Yoginīs</s>). The remaining [divine beings] are subsumed under these by similarity of nature.

children.translated_text: For example:
"That which wandered in the cave of <s>Hara</s>'s (Śiva's) matted locks, bearing the burden of crescent-moon-tip sprouts —
May that water of the celestial river (<s>Gaṅgā</s>) purify you, reverberating with the thunder-roar in the rocky groves of the <s>Himālaya</s>!"
<s>Vaidyādhara</s> (of the <s>Vidyādharas</s>):
"With subtle alliteration, possessing luster, with graceful expression and clarity,
With extensive compounds — know [this as] the speech of <s>Vidyādharas</s>."
For example:
"O you whose reddish feet shine forth at the tips of the toenails, illuminated by the rays of the lofty gems on the crowns of prostrating gods,
Whose form has <s>Anaṅga</s> (Kāma) burnt by the host of flames from the upward-gazing eyes, blazing with the magnificent radiance of the rising multitude of suns — salutations to you!"
Or for example:
"Wandering in the sky, golden as the clusters of <s>campaka</s> flowers in the <s>Nandana</s> grove, bright as the swarm of bees,
As if struck by a whirlwind, with radiance clearly visible — the beloved of <s>Rohaṇī</s> (the moon)."
<s>Gāndharva</s> (of the <s>Gandharvas</s>):
"With short and abundant compounds, adorned with clusters of words,
Grasped through the arrangement of essential meanings — [such is] the eloquence of the <s>Gandharvas</s>."
For example:
"Salutations to <s>Śiva</s>, to <s>Soma</s>, together with his host, together with his son,
Together with his bull, serpent, and trident, together with his skull-cup, together with <s>Indu</s> (the moon)."
<s>Yoginīgata</s> (of the <s>Yoginīs</s>):
"Mostly consisting of compounds and metaphors, with a sequence of words of profound meaning,
Abiding in the conventions of established doctrines — this is the speech of <s>Yoginīs</s>."
For example:
"O cloud that rains nectar, the sole fire for the fuel of suffering! O sole support-rope for those falling into the well of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence)!
O mirror of the kings of <s>yogins</s>! O radiance pervading the entire world! O supreme thief made manifest! O lord of heroes! Salutations to you!"
Due to its great power, even <s>Bhaujaṅgama</s> (serpent) [speech] is figuratively called divine.
"Clear, sweet, noble, partaking of both compound and expansive [forms],
Mostly consisting of words of gentle vigor — such is the speech of the serpent-beings (<s>Bhogins</s>)."
For example:
"Having received the well-crafted <s>vīṇā</s> (lute), pleasing to the ear, beautiful in form, with body adorned and brilliant with many jewels,

children.text: vidyādharendraḥ pratigṛhya vīṇāṃ pinākine gāyati maṅgalāni" //
children.translated_text: The lord of <s>Vidyādharas</s> sings auspicious songs for the bearer of the <s>Pināka</s> (Śiva)."

body.text:

yato nāṭakādāvīśvarādīnāṃ devānāṃ ca praveśe tacchāyāvanti vākyāni vidheyānīti divyam /
