"Although the sandal tree has been made by fate devoid of fruit and flower,
even so, by its own body alone, it removes the burning heat of others."
The third —

children.text: "daivāyatte hi phale kiṃ kriyatāmetadatra tu vadāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: "When fruit is in the hands of fate, what can be done? But this we say:
the tender shoots of the <s>aśoka</s> are not equal to the sprouts of other trees."

body.text: anekatra pravṛttavṛttīnāmekatrācaraṇaṃ niyamaḥ, tadyathā-samudreṣveva makarāḥ, tāmraparṇyāmeva mauktikāni /

children.translated_text: The first of these —
"Leading the clan-estate of the <s>Gotra</s> (lineage) to the status of a house, [bearing] the ocean stamped with the seal of his own name,
when the groups of claimants are stirring — the tusk-pride of the <s>makara</s> is praiseworthy!"

body.translated_text: Restriction is the confining to one place of that which occurs in many — for example: <s>makaras</s> (sea-creatures) only in oceans, pearls only in the <s>Tāmraparṇī</s> river.

children.translated_text: The second —

children.text: "kāmaṃ bhavantu sarito bhuvi sapratiṣṭhāḥ svādūni santu salilāni ca śuktayaśca /
children.translated_text: "Let the rivers on earth be well-established, let the waters be sweet, and let there be oysters;

children.text: etāṃ vihāya varavarṇini tāmraparṇīṃ nānyatra sambhavati mauktikakāmadhenuḥ" //
children.translated_text: but leaving aside this <s>Tāmraparṇī</s>, O lady of excellent complexion, the wish-fulfilling cow of pearls does not exist elsewhere."

body.text:
asato 'pi dravyasya nibandhanam /
tadyathā-muṣṭigrāhyatvaṃ sūcībhedyatvaṃ ca tamasaḥ, kumbhāpavāhyatvaṃ ca jyotsnāyāḥ /

children.translated_text: The first of these —
"As if the horizons are tapering to a point, as if the earth's circle is merely the reach of a footstep,
as if heaven is within arm's reach — darkness makes itself graspable by the fist."

body.translated_text: The binding of a non-existent substance — for example: darkness being graspable by the fist, and being pierceable by a needle; moonlight being carriable away in a pot.

children.translated_text: And also —
"Though the prison is enclosed, though the darkness cannot be pierced even by the tip of a needle,

children.text: mayi ca nimīlitanayane tathāpi kāntānanaṃ vyaktam" //
children.translated_text: and though my eyes are shut — even so, the face of my beloved is clearly [visible]."
The second —
"Bearing the beauty of a stream from the split bellies of <s>ketaka</s> flowers melted in a press, which formerly had a luster suitable for the art of stringing pearl garlands —

children.text: utsecyā kalaśībhirañjalipuṭairgrāhyā mṛṇālāṅkuraiḥ pātavyā ca śaśinyamugdhavibhave sā varttate candrikā" //
children.translated_text: that moonlight, which can be scooped up with pitchers, grasped in cupped palms, and drunk through lotus-stalk [straws], abides in the radiance of this innocent moon."

body.text: dravyasya sato 'nibandhanaṃ, tadyathā-kṛṣṇapakṣe satyā api jyotsnāyāḥ, śuklapakṣe tvandhakārasya /

children.translated_text: The first of these —
"The people there beheld with curiosity at the festival
<s>Balabhadra</s> and <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), like the bright and dark fortnights."

body.translated_text: The non-binding of an existing substance — for example: [denying] moonlight in the dark fortnight even though it exists, and [denying] darkness in the bright fortnight.

children.translated_text: The second —
"Month after month, the moonlight is the same in both the bright and dark fortnights;
in one of them, the whiteness that prevails — that is fame, obtained by meritorious deeds."

body.text: dravyaniyamaḥ, tadyathā-malaya eva candanasthānaṃ, himavāneva bhūrjotpattisthānam /

children.translated_text: The first of these —
"Skilled in removing heat, the abode of serpents, dear to the gods —
nowhere other than <s>Malaya</s> mountain is the sandalwood tree seen."

body.translated_text: Restriction of substance — for example: sandalwood only on <s>Malaya</s> mountain, birch-bark only on the <s>Himavān</s>.

children.translated_text: The second —
"Where birch-bark leaves, inscribed with mineral ink, red as the spots of elephants,
beautiful, serve the purpose of love-letters for the <s>Vidyādhara</s> maidens."

body.text:
prakīrṇakadravyakavisamayastu, tadyathā-
kṣīrakṣārasamudrayoraikyaṃ sāgaramahāsamudrayośca /

children.translated_text: The first of these —
"Let <s>Hari</s> sleep [there], let <s>Ananta</s> be the jewel within, let <s>Lakṣmī</s> be born [from it] — we do not dispute this!

children.text: hā dūradūrasapayāstṛṣitasya jantoḥ kiṃ tvatra kūpapayasaḥ sa marorjaghanyaḥ" //
children.translated_text: Alas! For a thirsty creature far, far [from water], this [ocean] is worse than the water of a well, with its salt waters."

body.translated_text: And miscellaneous substance conventions — for example: the identity of the milk-ocean and the salt-ocean, and of the ocean (<s>sāgara</s>) and the great ocean (<s>mahāsamudra</s>).

children.translated_text: The second —
"With the furrowing of brows formed by the dancing waves, as if threatening the rivers,
he beheld before him the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, the beloved of the seven oceans."

body.text: asato 'pi kriyārthasya nibandhanam, yathā-cakravākamithunasya niśi bhinnataṭāśrayaṇaṃ, cakorāṇāṃ candrikāpānaṃ ca /

children.translated_text: The first of these —
"Contracting the full waters of rivers that possess watches [of the night], reducing the young ones of those named after chariot-wheels (<s>cakravāka</s>) —
has summer not done a service [by drying the rivers so that they need not separate]?"

body.translated_text: The binding of a non-existent action — for example: the <s>cakravāka</s> pair separating to opposite banks at night; <s>cakora</s> birds drinking moonlight.

children.translated_text: The second —

children.text: "etāstā malayopakaṇṭhasaritāmeṇākṣi rodhobhuvaś cāpābhyāsaniketanaṃ bhagavataḥ preyo manojanmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: "O doe-eyed one, these are the banks of the rivers near <s>Malaya</s>, the archery-practice ground of the blessed <s>Kāma</s> (god of love);

children.text: yāsu śyāmaniśāsu pītatamaso muktāmayīścandrikāḥ pīyante vivṛtordhvacañcu vicalatkaṇṭhaṃ cakorāṅganāḥ" //
children.translated_text: where in the dark nights, the <s>cakora</s> hens drink the pearl-like moonlight, with necks stretched upward and throats quivering, having consumed the darkness."

body.text: sato 'pi kriyārthasyānibandhanam, tadyathā-divā nīlotpalānāmavikāso, niśānimittaśca śophālikākusumānāvistraṃsaḥ /

children.translated_text: The first of these —
"Having drawn a leaf-design on the face of the beloved with fragrant dark <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood) paste, upon the face that momentarily honored the moon's disc,

children.text: jātaḥ punarvikasanāvasaro 'yamasyety uktvā sakho kuvalayaṃ śravaṇe cakāra" //
children.translated_text: saying 'This [blue lotus] now has an occasion to bloom again,' her friend placed the <s>kuvalaya</s> (blue lotus) on [the beloved's] ear."

body.translated_text: The non-binding of an existing action — for example: blue lotuses not blooming during the day; and <s>śephālikā</s> (night-jasmine) flowers not falling except at night.

children.translated_text: The second —
"In separation from you, I have been entirely burned all day long by the fierce rays of the sun" —

children.text: itīva duḥkhaṃ śaśine gadantī śephālikā roditi puṣpabāṣpaiḥ" //
children.translated_text: thus, as if telling her sorrow to the moon, the <s>śephālikā</s> (night-jasmine) weeps with flower-tears."

body.text: niyamastu, tadyathā-grīṣmādau sambhavato 'pi kokilānāṃ virutasya vasanta eva, mayūrāṇāṃ varṣāsveva virutasya nṛttasya ca nibandhaḥ /

children.translated_text: The first of these —
"In spring, the cuckoo, frightened by cold, sang in the forest;
the lotuses beneath the water rose up, as if eager to listen."

body.translated_text: Restriction [of action] — for example: binding the cuckoo's song only to spring, even though it occurs from summer onward; and binding the peacock's cry and dance only to the rainy season.

children.translated_text: The second —
"Spreading their tail-feathers in a circle, with sweet songs from their throats,
the peacocks dance when the season wears its garland of clouds."
This is the convention of poets regarding genus, substance, and action;
hereafter, the convention regarding qualities, then the celestial and subterranean [conventions], are described.

body.text: iti rājaśekharakṛtau kāvyamīmāṃsāyāṃ kavirahasye prathame 'dhikaraṇe kavisamaye jātidravyakriyāsamayasthāpanā nāma caturdaśo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourteenth chapter, entitled "Establishing Conventions of Genus, Substance, and Action in Poetic Convention," in the first section of the <s>Kavirahsya</s> (Secrets of the Poet) in the <s>Kāvyamīmāṃsā</s> composed by <s>Rājaśekhara</s>.

body.text: pañcadaśo 'dhyāyaḥ 15
body.translated_text: Chapter 15

body.text:
guṇasamayasthāpanā asatoguṇasya nibandhanam /
yathā-yaśohāsaprabhṛteḥ śauklyam, ayaśasaḥ pāpaprabhṛteśca kārṣṇyaṃ, krodhānurāgaprabhṛteśca raktatvam /

children.translated_text: Whiteness of fame —

children.text: "stemaḥ stoko 'pi nāṅge śvasitamavikalaṃ cakṣuṣāṃ saiva vṛttir madhyekṣīrābdhi magnāḥ sphuṭamatha ca vayaṃ ko 'yamīdṛkprakāraḥ /
children.translated_text: "Not even a little perspiration on the body, the breathing is normal, the function of the eyes is exactly the same, clearly we are plunged in the midst of a milk-ocean — what manner [of strangeness] is this?

children.text: itthaṃ digbhittirodhaḥkṣatavisaratayā māṃsalaistvadyaśobhiḥ stokāvasthānaduḥsthaistrijagati dhavale vismayante mṛgākṣyaḥ" //
children.translated_text: Thus, because your fame — fleshy and white — spreads through all the three worlds, breaking through the walls of the directions, the doe-eyed women, distressed by so little room remaining, are astonished at the whiteness of the three worlds."

body.translated_text: Establishing Quality Conventions. The binding of a non-existent quality — for example: whiteness of fame, laughter, etc.; blackness of infamy, sin, etc.; and redness of anger, passion, etc.

children.translated_text: Whiteness of laughter —
"From whose mouth, under the pretext of loud laughter, foam-white torrents
of milk-oceans flow out, as if consumed at the dissolution of the world."
Blackness of infamy —
"Your glories and the infamies of your enemies spread simultaneously,
like garlands of <s>mālatī</s> (jasmine) interwoven with petals of blue lotus, day after day."
Blackness of sin —
"The body of the one whose neck bore [the mark of] compassion turned dark, as if smeared by the lines of sword-rays with their spotless luster uprooted —
as if soiled by the impurity of sin born from the resolve to destroy the lineage of <s>Keśava</s> in a fit of sudden rage."
Redness of anger —
"By his body made pink by the spreading glow of anger, reflected on the floor-surface of the audience hall,
occupying the belly of the netherworld with its swelling <s>rasa</s> (flavor/emotion) — the earth trembled, as if with the rolling of an unsteady belly."
Redness of passion, for example —
"By your fame that spreads, mixed with the passion for [your] virtues,
half-<s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron) has suddenly appeared on the faces of the bride-directions."

body.text:
sato 'pi guṇasyānibandhanam, (yathā)-
kundakuḍmalānāṃ kāmidantānāṃ ca raktatvaṃ, kamalamukulaprabhṛteśca haritatvaṃ, priyaṅguṣuṣpāṇāṃ ca pītatvam /

children.translated_text: The non-redness of <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) buds and so forth —
"Illuminated from within by his smiles at the tips of <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) buds,
his <s>Sarasvatī</s> (speech), of pure complexion, appeared as though bathed [in whiteness]."

body.translated_text: Even when a quality exists, its non-depiction [is a poetic convention]. As [illustrated by]: the redness of <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) buds and the teeth of lovers, the greenness of lotus buds and the like, and the yellowness of <s>priyaṅgu</s> (beauty-berry) blossoms.

children.translated_text: The non-greenness of lotus buds —
"With a tusk that touches the bewilderment of the upright-bellied <s>puṇḍarīka</s> (white lotus) bud, as a weapon for lifting up the earth submerged in the briny ocean,

while the hosts of gods and demons were agitated at that time with a towering uproar — may the form of <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) in the sport of the primeval boar (<s>Ādivarāha</s>), reaching up to the clouds, protect you!"
The non-yellowness of <s>priyaṅgu</s> (beauty-berry) blossoms —
"The dark-as-<s>priyaṅgu</s> cluster of breasts, piercing the ocean,
as if to adorn them, produces a wealth of lustrous pearls."

body.text: guṇaniyamastu tadyathā-sāmānyopādāne māṇikyānāṃ śoṇatā, puṣpāṇāṃ śuklatā, meghānāṃ śuklatā, meghānāṃ kṛṣṇatā ca /

children.translated_text: Of these, the first —
"Gathered in the dense dark rows of trees on the banks, constantly brought in heaps by travelers,
O long-eyed one, those [rubies] of yours bear here some resemblance to the orb of the sun crying out from the belly of a rain-cloud."

body.translated_text: The restriction of qualities is as follows — when mentioned generically: the redness of rubies, the whiteness of flowers, the whiteness of clouds, and the blackness of clouds.

children.translated_text: The whiteness of flowers —
"If a flower were set upon a coral shoot, or a pearl placed upon a radiant coral,
then it might imitate that bright smile of hers, its radiance spread over [her] lip-and-brow."
The blackness of clouds —
"The lord of aerial chariots, his sacrificial altar purified by cloud-dark hair,
shone like a heap of jewels with a great sapphire (<s>mahendranīla</s>) in the middle."

body.text: kṛṣṇanīlayoḥ, kṛṣṇaharitayoḥ, kṛṣṇaśyāmayoḥ, pītaraktayoḥ, śuklagaurayorekatvena nibandhanaṃ ca kavisamayaḥ /

children.translated_text: How is the identity of black and blue [established]? —
"Having swiftly crossed the river whose sandy banks are followed even by the ears, by southern women, having crossed its waters on both banks adorned with garlands of waves,

children.text: tataḥ sahyasyoccaiḥ svasalilanivaho bhāti nīlaḥ sa yasyāḥ priyasyāṃse pīne lulita iva ghanaḥ keśapāśaḥ sukeśyāḥ" //
children.translated_text: then from the heights of <s>Sahya</s> (the Western Ghats), that stream of its own waters appears blue — like the dark mass of hair, tossed about, on the plump shoulder of that beautiful-haired beloved."

body.translated_text: The poetic convention that black and blue, black and green, black and dark, yellow and red, white and fair are depicted as identical.

children.translated_text: The identity of black and green —
"The waters of the <s>Yamunā</s> resembling emerald, and the waters of the <s>Jāhnavī</s> (Ganges) clear as crystal stone —

children.text: tadubhayamudakaṃ punātu vo hariharayoriva saṅgataṃ vapuḥ" //
children.translated_text: may those two waters purify you, like the united forms of <s>Hari</s> and <s>Hara</s>."
The identity of black and dark —
"This, O beautiful one, is the <s>Nandana</s> (garden of <s>Indra</s>), with trees smooth as moonstone, bathed by the <s>Mandākinī</s>, on the pearl-stone terrace of <s>Meru</s>, it rejoices;

children.text: yatra śyāmaniśāsu muñcati milanmantaḥ pradoṣānilām uddāmāmarayoṣitāmabhirataṃ kalpadrumaścandrikām" //
children.translated_text: where in dark nights, the wish-granting trees release the unbound moonlight, beloved of the celestial women, mingling with the evening breeze."
The identity of yellow and red —
"With a streak of bright coral radiance, constantly dispelling darkness even at moonrise,
with a tusk tawny as broken gold, the primeval boar (<s>Ādivarāha</s>) [lifted] the disc of the earth, as it were."
The identity of white and fair —
"As he was about to mount the bull, white as <s>Kailāsa</s>, purified by the grace of placing [his] foot upon a pillar,

children.text: avehi māṃ kiṅkaramaṣṭamūrtteḥ kumbhodaraṃ nāma nikumbhaputram" //
children.translated_text: know me as the servant of the eight-formed lord (<s>Aṣṭamūrti</s>) — <s>Kumbhodara</s> by name, the son of <s>Nikumbha</s>."

body.text:
evaṃ varṇāntareṣvapi /
cakṣurāderanekavarṇopavarṇanam /

children.translated_text: Of these, the whiteness of the eye —

children.text: "tiṣṭhantyā janasaṅkule 'pi sudṛśā sāyaṃ gṛhaprāṅgaṇe taddvāraṃ mayi niḥsahālasatanau vīṅkhāmṛdu preṅkhati /
children.translated_text: "As she stood in the evening in the crowded courtyard of the house, that beautiful-eyed one, while I, exhausted and helpless, gently swayed at the door of that [courtyard],

children.text: hīnabhrānanayaiva lolasaralaṃ niḥśvasya tatrāntare premārdrāḥ śaśikhaṇḍapāṇḍimamuṣo muktāḥ kaṭākṣacchaṭāḥ" //
children.translated_text: with lowered brow, through that very glance, sighing straight and tremulously, in the interval, tender with love — she released volleys of sidelong glances, stealing the pallor of a crescent moon."

body.translated_text: Thus also with other colors. The depiction of the eye and other [features] with many colors and sub-colors.

children.translated_text: The darkness [of the eye] —

children.text: "atha pathi gamayitvā ramyakḷtpopakārye katicidavanipālaḥ śarvarīḥ śarvakalpaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Then having spent some nights on the road in a beautifully prepared [camp], the king, equal to <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>),
again entered <s>Ayodhyā</s>, whose windows were darkened like blue lotuses by the eyes of the women who had seen <s>Maithilī</s> (<s>Sītā</s>)."
The blackness [of the eye] —
"There, the courtesans with girdles jingling at every step, their hands weary from playfully waving jewel-colored, crease-adorned <s>cāmaras</s> (fly-whisks),

children.text: veśyāstvatto nakhapadasukhānprāpya varṣāgrabindū-nāmokṣyante tvayi madhukaraśreṇidīrghān kaṭākṣān" //
children.translated_text: having obtained from you the pleasure of nail-marks like the first drops of rain, they will cast upon you sidelong glances long as a row of bees."
The mixed coloring [of the eye] —

"Crossing beyond that, go forth among those whose practiced eyebrow-creeper play is charming, whose eyes shine above with the flash of upturned eyelids like those of the black antelope (<s>kṛṣṇaśāra</s>),
whose beauty rivals that of bees following tossed <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) flowers — making yourself an object of the eye-curiosity of the ladies of the ten cities (<s>Daśapura</s>)."

body.text: iti rājaśekharakṛtau kāvyamīmāṃsāyāṃ kavirahasye prathame 'dhikaraṇe guṇasamayasthāpanā pañcadaśo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fifteenth chapter, entitled 'The Establishment of Color Conventions' (<s>guṇasamayasthāpanā</s>), in the first section (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>), the Secret of Poets (<s>Kavirahasya</s>), of the <s>Kāvyamīmāṃsā</s> composed by <s>Rājaśekhara</s>.

body.text:
kavisamayaḥ
ṣoḍaśo 'dhyāyaḥ 16
body.translated_text: <s>Kavisamaya</s> (Poetic Conventions) — Sixteenth Chapter, 16

body.text: svargyapātālīyakavirahasya (samaya)sthāpanā bhaumavatsvargyo 'pi kavisamayaḥ, viśeṣastu candramasi śaśahariṇayoraikyam /

children.translated_text: As [illustrated by]: —

children.text: "mā bhaiḥ śaśāṅka? mama sīdhuni nāsti rāhuḥ khe rohiṇī vasati kātara kiṃ bibheṣi /
children.translated_text: "Fear not, O <s>Śaśāṅka</s> (Moon)! In my nectar there is no <s>Rāhu</s>; O timid one, <s>Rohiṇī</s> dwells in the sky — why do you fear?

children.text: prāyo vidagdhavanitānavasaṅgameṣu puṃsāṃ manaḥ pracalatīti kimatra citram" //
children.translated_text: It is mostly the case that at the intimate meetings of clever women, the minds of men waver — what wonder is there in this?"

body.translated_text: The establishment of the [poetic] convention regarding heavenly and netherworld [matters]. Like earthly conventions, there are also heavenly poetic conventions. The special feature is that in the moon, the hare and the deer are treated as identical.

children.translated_text: And as [illustrated by]: —
"The moon (<s>Candramā</s>) bears a deer placed in [his] lap, [hence] he is called <s>mṛgalāñchana</s> (deer-marked);
the lion, cruel by nature, is accompanied by deer [yet called] the lord of deer (<s>mṛgādhipa</s>)."
The identity of the <s>makara</s> (crocodile) and the fish on the banner of <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love). As [illustrated by]: —

children.text: "cāpaṃ puṣpamayaṃ gṛhāṇa makaraḥ ketuḥ samucchrīyatāṃ cetolakṣyabhidaśca pañca viśikhāḥ pāṇau punaḥ santu te /
children.translated_text: "Take up the flower-bow, let the <s>makara</s> (crocodile) banner be raised high, and let the five arrows that pierce the target of the mind be in your hand again;

children.text: dagdhā kāpi tavākṛteḥ pratikṛtiḥ kāmo 'si kiṃ gūhase rupaṃ darśaya nātra śaṅkarabhayaṃ sarve vayaṃ vaiṣṇavāḥ" //
children.translated_text: some image of your form has been burnt — you are <s>Kāma</s>, why do you hide? Show your form! There is no fear of <s>Śaṅkara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) here — we are all <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>!"
And as [illustrated by]: —

children.text: "mīnadhvajastvamasi no na ca ṣuṣpadhanvā keliprakāśa tava manmathatā tathāpi /
children.translated_text: "You are <s>Mīnadhvaja</s> (fish-bannered), not <s>Puṣpadhanvā</s> (flower-bowed) — O manifest in sport, yet your nature as <s>Manmatha</s> (the Agitator) remains;

children.text: itthaṃ tvayā virahitasya mayopalabdhāḥ kāntājanasya jananātha ciraṃ vilāpāḥ" //
children.translated_text: thus, O lord of men, I have heard for a long time the lamentations of the beloved women separated from you."
And as [illustrated by]: —
"The lord of the ocean, whose waters are churned by the falling wind, having turned around the fish-banner in fright at the roar,
crossing the terrible tide of the great ocean of the <s>Yādavas</s>, I shall lift up Mount <s>Droṇa</s> like the son of the Wind (<s>Hanumān</s>)."
The identity of <s>Atri</s>'s eye-born and the ocean-born moon —

children.text: "vandyā viśvasṛjo yugādiguravaḥ svāyambhuvāḥ satpa ye tatrātrirdivi sandadhe nayanajaṃ jyotiḥ sa candro 'bhavat /
children.translated_text: "Worthy of worship are the seven <s>Svāyambhuva</s> sages, the primordial teachers of the ages, the creators of the world; among them, <s>Atri</s> placed in the sky the light born from his eye — that became the moon;

children.text: ekā yasya śikhaṇḍamaṇḍanamaṇirdevasya śambhoḥ kalā śeṣābhyo 'mṛtamāpnuvanti ca sadā svāhāsvadhājīvinaḥ" //
children.translated_text: one <s>kalā</s> (digit) of that [moon] is the crest-jewel adorning the topknot of the god <s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), and from the remaining [digits] those who live on <s>svāhā</s> and <s>svadhā</s> offerings always obtain nectar."
Even though the moon on <s>Śiva</s>'s [head] has existed since long ages, it is [depicted as always] young —
"O swan of the celestial river adorned with garlands, O blossom of the crown-creeper of <s>Bhava</s> (<s>Śiva</s>),
O mirror-beauty of the coquetry of <s>Dākṣāyaṇī</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>) — may the crescent moon (<s>bālendukhaṇḍa</s>) purify you!"
And the embodiment of <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love). As [illustrated by]: —

children.text: "ayaṃ sa bhuvanatrayaprathitasaṃyamaḥ śaṅkaro bibhartti vapuṣādhunā virahakātaraḥ kāminīm /
children.translated_text: "This is that <s>Śaṅkara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), renowned in the three worlds for his self-restraint — yet he now holds in his body a woman, afflicted by separation;

children.text: anena kila nirjitā vayamiti priyāyāḥ karaṃ kareṇa paritāḍayan jayati jātahāsaḥ smaraḥ" //
children.translated_text: striking the hand of the beloved with his own hand, saying 'By this one, indeed, we were conquered!' — <s>Smara</s> (<s>Kāma</s>), having burst into laughter, triumphs!"
And as [illustrated by]: —

children.text: "dhanurmālā maurvī kvaṇadalikulaṃ lakṣyamabalā mano bhedyaṃ śabdaprabhṛti ya ime pañca viśikhāḥ /
children.translated_text: "His bow is a garland [of flowers], his bowstring is the humming swarm of bees, his target is the helpless mind, the point of penetration is sound, and these are the five arrows;

children.text: iyān jetuṃ yasya tribhuvanamanaṅgasya vibhavaḥ sa vaḥ kāmaḥ kāmāndiśatu dayitāpāṅgavasatiḥ" //
children.translated_text: such is the power of the bodiless <s>Anaṅga</s> (<s>Kāma</s>) to conquer the three worlds — may that <s>Kāma</s>, who dwells in the sidelong glances of the beloved, grant you your desires!"
The identity of the twelve <s>Ādityas</s> (solar deities) —

children.text: "yasyādho 'dhastathoparyupari niravadhi bhrābhyato viśvamaśvair āvṛttālātalīlāṃ racayati rayato maṇḍalaṃ caṇḍadhāmnaḥ /
children.translated_text: "He below whom and above whom the universe extends without limit, who with his horses creates the sport of revolving, speeding as a disc of fierce splendor on all sides,

children.text: so 'vyāduttatpakārttasvarasaralaśarasparddhibhirddhāmadaṇḍair uddaṇḍaiḥ prāpayanvaḥ prayuratamatamaḥ stomamastaṃ samastam" //
children.translated_text: may he, the exalted one, sending forth with his towering rays of brilliance — rivals to the swift, straight arrows of the afflicted — drive the entire mass of darkness to its setting for you!"
And [the identity] of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>. As [illustrated by]: —

children.text: "yena dhvastamanobhavena balijitkāyaḥ purāstrīkṛto yo gaṅgāṃ ca dadhe 'ndhakakṣayakaro yo barhipatrapriyaḥ /
children.translated_text: "He by whom, having destroyed <s>Manobhava</s> (<s>Kāma</s>), the body of the conqueror of <s>Bali</s> was once made into a woman; he who held the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, the destroyer of <s>Andhaka</s>; he who is fond of peacock feathers;

children.text: yasyāhuḥ śaśimacchirohara iti stutyaṃ ca nāmāmarāḥ so 'vyādaṣṭabhujaṅgahāravalayastvāṃ sarvadomādhavaḥ" //
children.translated_text: he whose praiseworthy name the gods declare as '<s>Śaśimacchirohara</s>' (bearer of the hare-marked moon on the head) — may that <s>Mādhava</s>, whose bracelet is a coil of eight serpents, protect you who are the giver of all!"

body.text: evaṃ dāmodaraśeṣakūrmādeḥ /

children.translated_text: And [the identity] of <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) and prosperity. As [illustrated by]: —

children.text: "dormanderitamandareṇa jaladherutthāpitā yā svayaṃ yāṃ bhūtvā kamaṭhaḥ purāṇakakudanyastāmudastabhbhayat /
children.translated_text: "She who was raised from the ocean by herself when the <s>Mandara</s> [mountain] was churned by the arm, she whom, having become a tortoise, [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] formerly supported, placing her on his ancient hump,

children.text: tāṃ lakṣyīṃ puruṣottamaḥ punarasau līlāñcitabhrūlatā-nirdeśaiḥ samavīviśatpraṇayināṃ geheṣu doṣṇi kṣitim" //
children.translated_text: that <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Puruṣottama</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) himself, with the playful indications of his gracefully arched eyebrow-creeper, caused to enter the homes of his devotees — [that is,] the earth, with his arms."

body.translated_text: Likewise for <s>Dāmodara</s>, <s>Śeṣa</s>, <s>Kūrma</s>, and so on.

body.text: bhaumasvargyavatpātālīyo 'pi kavisamayaḥ /

children.translated_text: Of these, the identity of <s>nāgas</s> (serpent-deities) and <s>sarpas</s> (serpents) —

children.text: "he nāgarāja bahumasya nitambabhāgaṃ bhogena gāḍhamabhiveṣṭaya mandarādreḥ /
children.translated_text: "O <s>Nāgarāja</s> (King of Serpents), greatly honoring the hip-region, tightly encircle the <s>Mandara</s> mountain with your coils;
having endured the unbearable sport of the yoke of the bull-vehicled one (<s>Śiva</s>) in the posture of a couch-binding — what excessive burden is there for you?"

body.translated_text: Like earthly and heavenly [conventions], there are also netherworld poetic conventions.

body.text: daityadānavāsurāṇāmaikyam, yathā tatra hiraṇyākṣahiraṇyakaśipruprahlādavirocanabalibāṇādayo daityāḥ, vipracittiśambaranamucipulomaprabhṛtayo dānavāḥ, valavṛtravikṣurastavṛṣaparvādayāsurāḥ /

children.translated_text: Their identity, as [illustrated by]: —

"Victorious are the dust-particles from the feet of <s>Tryambaka</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), the destroyer of worldly bondage, who are caressed by the crowns of <s>Bāṇāsura</s>, who kiss the crest-jewel diadem of the ten-faced one (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>),
who rest at the tips of the crests of the lords of gods and demons!"

body.translated_text: The identity of <s>Daityas</s>, <s>Dānavas</s>, and <s>Asuras</s>. As [illustrated by]: among these, <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>, <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, <s>Prahlāda</s>, <s>Virocana</s>, <s>Bali</s>, <s>Bāṇa</s>, and others are <s>Daityas</s>; <s>Vipracitti</s>, <s>Śambara</s>, <s>Namuci</s>, <s>Puloma</s>, and others are <s>Dānavas</s>; <s>Vala</s>, <s>Vṛtra</s>, <s>Vikṣura</s>, <s>Astavṛṣaparva</s>, and others are <s>Asuras</s>.

children.translated_text: And as [illustrated by]: —
"Who could conquer <s>Mīnadhvaja</s> (<s>Kāma</s>), whose essence is the thunderbolt-arrow of the demon <s>Śambara</s>, whose arm-staves are reddened by the rays of his armlet-gems,
whose broad shoulders bear the leaf-marks from the breasts of his clinging beloved — the conqueror of the three worlds!"
And as [illustrated by]: —
"There is a <s>Daitya</s> named <s>Hayagrīva</s>, whose arms, in the houses of his friends,
display his might — like splendors smiling with white parasols."
And as [illustrated by] — addressed to <s>Hayagrīva</s>: —
"Is not this arm of the lord of the <s>Dānavas</s> being led again
to serve as an ally of <s>Kṛtānta</s> (Death) in accomplishing his purposes of destruction?"
And as [illustrated by]: —
"In this great assembly of <s>Asuras</s>, there is not a single <s>Asura</s>
whose chest has not been consecrated by the striking of the thunderbolt."
Thus there are other distinctions too —

children.text: "so 'yaṃ kavīnāṃ samayaḥ kāvye sutpa iva sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: "This convention of the poets stands in poetry like a thread;
it has now been explained here by us to the best of our understanding."

body.text: iti rājaśekharakṛtau kāvyamīmāṃsāyāṃ kavirahasye prathame 'dhikaraṇe svargyapātālīyakavisamayasthāpanā ṣoḍaśo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the sixteenth chapter, entitled 'The Establishment of Heavenly and Netherworld Poetic Conventions' (<s>svargyapātālīyakavisamayasthāpanā</s>), in the first section (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>), the Secret of Poets (<s>Kavirahasya</s>), of the <s>Kāvyamīmāṃsā</s> composed by <s>Rājaśekhara</s>.

body.text: saptadaśo 'dhyāyaḥ 17
body.translated_text: Seventeenth Chapter, 17

body.text:
deśakālavibhāgaḥ tatra deśavibhāgaḥ deśaṃ kālaṃ ca vibhajamānaḥ kavirnārthadarśanadiśi daridrāti /
jagajjagadekadeśāśca deśaḥ /
"dyāvāpṛthivyātmakamekaṃ jagat" ityeke /

children.translated_text: They say —

children.text: "halamagu balasyaiko 'naḍvānharasya na lāṅgalaṃ kramaparimitā bhūmirviṣṇorna gaurna ca lāṅgalam /
children.translated_text: "The only ox of <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) is his plough-animal, he has no [real] plough; <s>Hari</s>'s (<s>Viṣṇu</s>'s) land is measured by [his] steps, he has no ox and no plough;

children.text: pravahati kṛṣirnādyāpyeṣāṃ dvitīyagavaṃ vinā jagati sakale nedṛgdṛṣṭaṃ daridrakuṭumbakam" //
children.translated_text: the farming of these [two] does not proceed even now without a second ox — in the whole world, never has such a destitute household been seen!"

body.translated_text: The division of place and time. Therein, the division of place: a poet who divides place and time does not become destitute in the direction of perceiving meaning. The world, and a part of the world, is 'place' (<s>deśa</s>). "The world is one, consisting of heaven and earth" — say some.

body.text: "divaspṛthivyau dve jagatī" ityapare /

children.translated_text: They say —
"As far as his imperishable fame fills the two worlds (heaven and earth),
so long does this meritorious one surely abide in the abode of the gods."

body.translated_text: "Heaven and earth are the two worlds" — say others.

body.text: "svargamartyapātālabhedāttrīṇi jaganti" ityeke /

children.translated_text: They say —
"You alone, O Lord, are the netherworld; you are the boundary of the directions;
you are the realm of the immortals, the wind, and the earth — you alone serve as the three worlds."

body.translated_text: "The worlds are three, distinguished as heaven, earth, and netherworld" — say some.

body.text: "tānyeva bhūrbhruvaḥsvaḥ"ityanye /

children.translated_text: They say —
"Obeisance to the one who, as if from the weariness of bearing the sustenance of the three worlds,
reclines on the couch of the body of <s>Nāganātha</s> (the Lord of Serpents, <s>Śeṣa</s>), the wielder of the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow."

body.translated_text: "Those same [three] are [also called] <s>bhūḥ</s>, <s>bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>svaḥ</s>" — say others.

body.text: "maharjanastapaḥsatyamityetaiḥ saha satpa" ityapare /

children.translated_text: They say —
"She who holds up the broad-hipped slopes of the earth, who carries the rain clouds with their moving banner-hands,
this row of palaces with lofty peaks shines forth, belonging to <s>Harṣa</s> whose great fame has spread through the seven worlds."

body.translated_text: "With the addition of <s>mahar</s>, <s>jana</s>, <s>tapas</s>, and <s>satya</s> [lokas], there are seven" — say others.

body.text: "tāni satpabhirvāyuskandhaiḥ saha caturdaśa" iti kecit /

children.translated_text: On that they say —
"He whose limitless and unsupported display of curious wonders stands forth,
that first one, in the form of <s>Kūrma</s> (the Tortoise), prevails here — the root-bulb of the creeper of the fourteen worlds."

body.translated_text: "Those [worlds] are fourteen, together with the seven [upper worlds] and the wind-regions" — say some.

body.text: "tāni satpabhiḥ pātālaiḥ sahaikaviṃśatiḥ" iti kecit /

children.translated_text: On that they say —
"Radiant like the necklace that is the laughter of <s>Hara</s>, like the abode of <s>Harā</s>, like the garland of <s>Hara</s>,
may your glories anoint the twenty-one worlds."

body.translated_text: "Those [worlds] are twenty-one, together with the seven <s>pātālas</s> (netherworlds)" — say some.

body.text:
"sarvamupapannam" iti yāyāvarīyaḥ /
aviśeṣavivakṣā yadekayati, viśeṣavivakṣātvanekayati /

children.translated_text: Among these, <s>Bhūrloka</s> (the earthly world) is the earth.
Therein are seven great <s>dvīpas</s> (continents).

children.text: "jambūdvīpaḥ sarvamadhye tataśca plakṣo nāmnā śālmalo 'taḥ kuśo 'taḥ /
children.translated_text: "<s>Jambūdvīpa</s> is in the very center, then <s>Plakṣa</s> by name, then <s>Śālmala</s>, then <s>Kuśa</s>,

children.text: krauñcaḥ śākaḥ puṣkaraścetyathaiṣāṃ bāhyā bāhyā saṃsthitirmaṇḍalībhiḥ" //
children.translated_text: <s>Krauñca</s>, <s>Śāka</s>, and <s>Puṣkara</s> — thus the outer ones are situated successively in concentric rings."

body.translated_text: "All [views] are justified" — says <s>Yāyāvarīya</s>. When no distinction is intended, one uses the singular; but when distinction is intended, one uses the plural.

children.text: "lāvaṇo rasamayaḥ surodakaḥ sārpiṣo dadhijalaḥ payaḥ payāḥ /
children.translated_text: "The salt ocean, the ocean of sugarcane juice, the ocean of wine, the ocean of clarified butter, the ocean of curds, the ocean of milk,
and the ocean of sweet water — these seven, surrounding them, are established [between them]."

body.text: "eka evāyaṃ lāvaṇaḥ samudraḥ" ityeke /

children.translated_text: On that they say —

"The continents here are eighteen, the earth too is spread out with nine divisions of its own parts; there is one single ocean whose waters extend to the horizons — this is a vast kingdom of the gods.

children.text: kasminnapyājikelivyatikaravijayopārjite vīravīrye paryātpaṃ me na dātuṃ tadidamiti dhiyā vedhase yaścukopa" //
children.translated_text: In some contest of battle-sport, having earned heroic valor through the exertion of victory, [the king] became wrathful toward <s>Brahmā</s>, thinking 'this is not enough for me to give away.'"

body.translated_text: "There is only one ocean, the salt ocean" — say some.

body.text: "trayaḥ" ityanye /

children.translated_text: On that they say —
"By [the king] whose valor, which shattered mountains exceedingly and contemptuously overpowered the three oceans,
was dispersed with its obstacles removed — the wind released at the end of the <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age) followed after [it]."

body.translated_text: "[There are] three [oceans]" — say others.

children.translated_text: Or alternatively —

children.text: "mātāṅgānāmabhāve madamalinamukhaiḥ prātpamāśākarīndraiḥ jāte rantāpahāre diśi diśi tatayo bhānti cintāmaṇīnām /
children.translated_text: "In the absence of elephants, when the first guardian-elephants of the directions with their faces dark with rut were captured, rows of <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gems) shine in every direction as a substitute for delight;

children.text: chinneṣūdyānavāpītaruṣu viracitāḥ kalpavṛkṣā ripūṇāṃ yasyodañcattrivelāvalayaphalabhujāṃ mānasī siddhirāsīt" //
children.translated_text: when the garden and pond trees of the enemies were cut down, <s>kalpavṛkṣas</s> (wish-fulfilling trees) were fashioned — such was the mental <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) of him who enjoyed the fruits of the girdle of the three-shored [ocean]."

body.text: "catvāraḥ" ityapare /

children.translated_text: On that they say —
"Having transgressed even <s>Meru</s>, the king of mountains, adorned with creeper-garlands made of the waves of the four oceans,
his fame has gone somewhere beyond."

body.translated_text: "[There are] four [oceans]" — say yet others.

body.text:
"bhinnābhiprāyatayayā sarvamupapannam" iti yāyavarīyaḥ /
satpasamrudrīvādinastu śāstrādanapetā eva /

children.translated_text: On that they say —
"When the waters of the seven oceans, which were the leftover water of <s>Agastya's</s> drinking,
were being crossed even by <s>Keśava</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) in a moment, he appeared purified."

body.translated_text: "All is justified by the difference in viewpoints" — says <s>Yāyāvarīya</s>. But those who maintain seven oceans are indeed not deviating from the <s>śāstra</s> (authoritative treatise).

children.translated_text: In the middle of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, the foremost among mountains, the golden king of mountains named <s>Meru</s>,
who is the repository of all embodied herbs, and who is the abode of all the gods.
"Having made that [<s>Meru</s>] as the axis, by the lotus-born god (<s>Brahmā</s>),
the creation of the universe was made — horizontally, upward, and downward."

body.text:
sa bhagavānmerurādyo varṣaparvataḥ /
tasya caturdiśamilāvṛtaṃ varṣam /
tasyottareṇa trayo varṣagirayaḥ, nīlaḥ śvetaḥ śṛṅgavāṃśca /
ramyakaṃ, hiraṇyayam, uttarāḥ kurava iti ca krameṇa trīṇi teṣāṃ varṣāṇi /
dakṣiṇenāpi traya eva niṣadho hemakūṭo himavāṃśca /
harivarṣaṃ, kiṃpuruṣaṃ, bhāratamiti ca trīṇi varṣāṇi /
tatredaṃ bhārataṃ varṣamasya ca nava bhedāḥ /
indradvīpaḥ, kaserumān, tāmraparṇo, gabhastimān, nāgadvīpaḥ, saumyo, gandharvoṃ, varuṇaḥ, kumārīdvīpaścāyaṃ navamaḥ /
pañcaśatāni jalaṃ, pañca sthalamiti vibhāgena pratyekaṃ yojanasahasrāvadhayo dakṣiṇātsamudrādadrirājaṃ himavantaṃ yāvatparasparamagamyāste /
tānyetāni yo jayati sa sabhrāḍityucyate /
kumārīpurātprabhṛti bindusaro 'vadhi yojanānāṃ daśaśatī cakravarttikṣetram /
tāṃ vijayamānaścakravarttī bhavati /

children.translated_text: The insignia of a <s>cakravartin</s> are —
"The discus, the chariot, the jewel, the queen, the treasure, the horse, and the elephant —
these are declared to be the seven jewels (<s>ratnas</s>) of all <s>cakravartins</s>."

body.translated_text: That blessed <s>Meru</s> is the foremost <s>varṣaparvata</s> (boundary mountain). On its four sides is the <s>Ilāvṛta</s> <s>varṣa</s> (region). To its north are three boundary mountains: <s>Nīla</s>, <s>Śveta</s>, and <s>Śṛṅgavān</s>. <s>Ramyaka</s>, <s>Hiraṇmaya</s>, and <s>Uttarāḥ Kuravaḥ</s> (the Northern <s>Kurus</s>) are, in order, the three <s>varṣas</s> (regions) between them. To the south also are three: <s>Niṣadha</s>, <s>Hemakūṭa</s>, and <s>Himavān</s>. <s>Harivarṣa</s>, <s>Kiṃpuruṣa</s>, and <s>Bhārata</s> are the three <s>varṣas</s>. Here, this is the <s>Bhārata varṣa</s>, and it has nine divisions: <s>Indradvīpa</s>, <s>Kaserumān</s>, <s>Tāmraparṇa</s>, <s>Gabhastimān</s>, <s>Nāgadvīpa</s>, <s>Saumya</s>, <s>Gāndharva</s>, <s>Vāruṇa</s>, and this ninth one, <s>Kumārīdvīpa</s>. With the division of five hundred [<s>yojanas</s>] of water and five hundred of land, each extending up to a thousand <s>yojanas</s>, from the southern ocean to the king of mountains <s>Himavān</s>, they are mutually inaccessible. He who conquers all these is called a sovereign (<s>samrāṭ</s>). From <s>Kumārīpura</s> to <s>Bindusaras</s>, a distance of a thousand <s>yojanas</s>, is the domain of a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal emperor). He who conquers that becomes a <s>cakravartin</s>.

children.translated_text: And in this <s>Kumārīdvīpa</s> —
"<s>Vindhya</s> and <s>Pāriyātra</s>, <s>Śuktimān</s>, <s>Ṛkṣaparvata</s>,
<s>Mahendra</s>, <s>Sahya</s>, and <s>Malaya</s> — these are the seven <s>kulaparvatāḥ</s> (principal mountain ranges)."

body.text: tatra vindhyādayaḥ pratītasvarupāḥ, malayaviśeṣāstu catvāraḥ /

children.translated_text: Among these, the first —
"From the base of the staff-like [trunks], wound by serpents, of the auspicious sandalwood trees that delight people,
combined with <s>kakkola</s>, <s>kailāma</s>, and <s>marica</s> (pepper) — it is the birthplace of <s>jātī</s> (jasmine) trees."

body.translated_text: Among these, <s>Vindhya</s> and others are well-known in their own form, but there are four varieties of <s>Malaya</s>.

children.translated_text: The second —
"At its foothill, the river <s>Tāmraparṇī</s> worships the supreme wish-fulfilling cow of pearls;
<s>Kumbhodbhava</s> (<s>Agastya</s>), the lord of gems, the great treasure-house of jewels, purifies that <s>Malaya</s>.

children.text: tatra drumā vidrumanāmadheyā vaṃśeṣi muktāphalajanma tatra /
children.translated_text: There the trees bear the name of coral, and among the bamboos, pearls are born;
with the roaring from the throats of fierce lions in rut, the <s>dhanasāra</s> (camphor) trees burst open in that [mountain]."
The third —
"The pleasure-ground of all the gods, the abode of <s>Gauri</s> and the bull among sages,
with ever-fruitful flowers, creepers, and sprouts — that <s>Malaya</s> there is the root of wonder."
The fourth —
"There, with palace-rows adorned with parapets brilliant with gold and gems,
with door-bolts bearing the marks of the lord of the gods — that which is <s>Laṅkā</s>, the royal capital of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

body.text:
pravarttate
kokilanādahetuḥ puṣpaprasūḥ pañcamajanmadāyī tebhyaścaturbhyo 'pi vasantamitramudaṅmukho dakṣiṇamātariśvā" //
body.translated_text: There proceeds the southern wind blowing northward, the friend of spring, the cause of the cuckoo's song, the producer of flowers, the giver of birth to the fifth [season] — from all four of those [<s>Malayas</s>]."

body.text:
pūrvāparayoḥ samudrayorhimavadvindhyayośvāntaramāryāvarttaḥ /
tasmiṃścāturvarṇyaṃ cāturāśramyaṃ ca /
yanmūlaśca sadācāraḥ /
tatratyo vyavahāraḥ prāyeṇa kavīnām /
tatra vārāṇasyāḥ purataḥ pūrvadeśaḥ /
yatrāṅgakaliṅgakosalatosa(śaṣa) lotkalamagadhamudgaravidehanepālapuṇḍra prāgjyotiṣatāmalitpakamaladamallavarttakasuhyabrahyottaraprabhṛtayo janapadāḥ /
bṛhadgṛhalohitagiricakoradarduranepālakāmarupādayaḥ parvatāḥ /
śoṇalauhityau nadau /
gaṅgākaratoyākapiśādyāśca nadyaḥ /
lavalīgranthiparṇakāgurudrākṣākastūrikādīnāmutpādaḥ /
māhiṣmatyāḥ parato dakṣiṇāpathaḥ /
yatra mahārāṣṭramāhiṣakāśmakavidarbhakuntalakrathakaiśikasūrpārakakāñcīkeralakāveramuralavānavāsakasiṃhalacoḍadaṇḍa kapāṇḍyapallavagāṅganāśikyakauṅkaṇakolla (la) girivallaraprabhṛtayo janapadāḥ /
vindhyadakṣiṇapādamahendramalayamekalapālamañjarasahyaśrīparvatādayaḥ parvatāḥ /
narmadātāpīpayoṣṇīgodāvarīkāverībhaimarathīveṇākṛṣṇaveṇīvañjurātuṅgabhadrātāmraparṇyutpalāvatīrāvaṇagaṅgādyā nadyaḥ /
tadutpattirmalayotpattyā vyākhyātā /
devasabhāyāḥ parataḥ paścāddeśaḥ /
tatra debasabhasurāṣṭradaśerakatravaṇabhṛgukacchakacchīyānarttarbudabrabahyaṇavāhayavanaprabhṛtayo janapadāḥ /
govardhanagirinagaradevasabhamālyaśikharārbudādayāśca parvatāḥ /
sarasvatīśvabhravatīvārtadhnīmahāhiḍimbādyā nadyaḥ /
karīrapīluguggulukharjūrakarabhādīnāmutpādaḥ /
pṛthūdakātparata uttarāpathaḥ /
yatra śakakekayavokkāṇahūṇavāṇāyujakāmbojavālīkavalavalimpākakulūtakīrataṅgaṇatuṣāraturuṣkabarbaraharahūravahūhūkasahuḍa haṃsamārgaramaṭhakarakaṇṭhaprabhṛtayo janapadāḥ /
himālayakalindrendrakīlacandrācalādayaḥ parvatāḥ /
gaṅgāsindhusarasvatīśatadrucandrabhāgāyamunerāvatīvitastāvipāśākuhūtevi kādyā nadyaḥ /
saraladevadārudrākṣākuṅkumacarājinasauvīrasrotojjanasaindhavavaidūryaturaṅgāṇāmutpādaḥ /
teṣāṃ madhye madhyadeśa iti kavivyavahāraḥ /
na cāyaṃ nānugantā śāstrārthasya /

children.translated_text: On that they say —
"That which lies between <s>Himavān</s> and <s>Vindhya</s>, and east of <s>Vinaśana</s>,
and west of <s>Prayāga</s> — that is declared to be <s>Madhyadeśa</s> (the Middle Country)."

body.translated_text: Between the eastern and western oceans, and between <s>Himavān</s> and <s>Vindhya</s>, is <s>Āryāvarta</s>. In it are the four <s>varṇas</s> (social classes) and the four <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life). And right conduct (<s>sadācāra</s>) is its foundation. The affairs of that region are mostly [the subject] of poets. There, to the east of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> is the eastern region, where are the territories of <s>Aṅga</s>, <s>Kaliṅga</s>, <s>Kosala</s>, <s>Tośala</s>, <s>Utkala</s>, <s>Magadha</s>, <s>Mudgara</s>, <s>Videha</s>, <s>Nepāla</s>, <s>Puṇḍra</s>, <s>Prāgjyotiṣa</s>, <s>Tāmalipta</s>, <s>Kamala</s>, <s>Damalla</s>, <s>Varttaka</s>, <s>Suhya</s>, <s>Brahyottara</s>, and others. The mountains are <s>Bṛhadgṛha</s>, <s>Lohitagiri</s>, <s>Cakora</s>, <s>Dardura</s>, <s>Nepālaka</s>, <s>Kāmarūpa</s>, and others. The rivers are <s>Śoṇa</s> and <s>Lauhitya</s>. And the rivers <s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Karatoyā</s>, <s>Kapiśā</s>, and others. The products are <s>lavalī</s>, <s>granthiparṇaka</s>, <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood), <s>drākṣā</s> (grapes), <s>kastūrikā</s> (musk), and so forth. Beyond <s>Māhiṣmatī</s> is the <s>Dakṣiṇāpatha</s> (the southern route), where are the territories of <s>Mahārāṣṭra</s>, <s>Māhiṣaka</s>, <s>Aśmaka</s>, <s>Vidarbha</s>, <s>Kuntala</s>, <s>Krathakaiśika</s>, <s>Sūrpāraka</s>, <s>Kāñcī</s>, <s>Kerala</s>, <s>Kāvera</s>, <s>Murala</s>, <s>Vānavāsaka</s>, <s>Siṃhala</s>, <s>Coḍa</s>, <s>Daṇḍaka</s>, <s>Pāṇḍya</s>, <s>Pallava</s>, <s>Gāṅga</s>, <s>Nāśikya</s>, <s>Kauṅkaṇa</s>, <s>Kolla</s>, <s>Girivallara</s>, and others. The mountains are <s>Vindhya</s>, <s>Dakṣiṇapāda</s>, <s>Mahendra</s>, <s>Malaya</s>, <s>Mekala</s>, <s>Pālamañjara</s>, <s>Sahya</s>, <s>Śrīparvata</s>, and others. The rivers are <s>Narmadā</s>, <s>Tāpī</s>, <s>Payoṣṇī</s>, <s>Godāvarī</s>, <s>Kāverī</s>, <s>Bhaimarathī</s>, <s>Veṇā</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇaveṇī</s>, <s>Vañjurā</s>, <s>Tuṅgabhadrā</s>, <s>Tāmraparṇī</s>, <s>Utpalāvatī</s>, <s>Rāvaṇagaṅgā</s>, and others. The products of that region have been described along with the products of <s>Malaya</s>. Beyond <s>Devasabhā</s> is the western region, where are the territories of <s>Devasabhā</s>, <s>Surāṣṭra</s>, <s>Daśeraka</s>, <s>Travaṇa</s>, <s>Bhṛgukaccha</s>, <s>Kacchīya</s>, <s>Ānarta</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Brabahyaṇa</s>, <s>Vāhayavana</s>, and others. The mountains are <s>Govardhana</s>, <s>Girinagara</s>, <s>Devasabhā</s>, <s>Mālyaśikhara</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, and others. The rivers are <s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>Śvabhravatī</s>, <s>Vārtadhnī</s>, <s>Mahāhiḍimbā</s>, and others. The products are <s>karīra</s>, <s>pīlu</s>, <s>guggulu</s>, <s>kharjūra</s> (dates), <s>karabha</s>, and so forth. Beyond <s>Pṛthūdaka</s> is the <s>Uttarāpatha</s> (the northern route), where are the territories of <s>Śaka</s>, <s>Kekaya</s>, <s>Vokkāṇa</s>, <s>Hūṇa</s>, <s>Vāṇāyuja</s>, <s>Kāmboja</s>, <s>Vālīka</s>, <s>Valavalimpāka</s>, <s>Kulūta</s>, <s>Kīra</s>, <s>Taṅgaṇa</s>, <s>Tuṣāra</s>, <s>Turuṣka</s>, <s>Barbara</s>, <s>Harahūra</s>, <s>Vahūhūka</s>, <s>Sahuḍa</s>, <s>Haṃsamārgara</s>, <s>Maṭhakarakaṇṭha</s>, and others. The mountains are <s>Himālaya</s>, <s>Kalinda</s>, <s>Indrakīla</s>, <s>Candrācala</s>, and others. The rivers are <s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Sindhu</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>Śatadru</s>, <s>Candrabhāgā</s>, <s>Yamunā</s>, <s>Irāvatī</s>, <s>Vitastā</s>, <s>Vipāśā</s>, <s>Kuhū</s>, <s>Tevikā</s>, and others. The products are <s>sarala</s> (pine), <s>devadāru</s> (cedar), <s>drākṣā</s> (grapes), <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron), <s>carma</s> (leather), <s>ajina</s> (deer-skin), <s>sauvīra</s>, <s>srotojjana</s>, <s>saindhava</s> (rock-salt), <s>vaidūrya</s> (beryl), and horses. Among these, the central region is called <s>Madhyadeśa</s> in poetic usage. And this [usage] does not fail to follow the sense of the <s>śāstra</s>.

children.text: tatra ca ye deśāḥ parvatāḥ sarito dravyāṇāmutpādaśca tatprasiddhisiddhamiti na nirdiṣṭam /
children.translated_text: Therein, the regions, mountains, rivers, and products [of each area] are well-established by common knowledge, and hence have not been specified [further].
As for the regions, mountains, and rivers of the other <s>dvīpas</s> (continents) —
they are not much employed by poets, and hence have not been deeply considered.

body.text:
"vinaśanaprayāgayorgaṅgāyamunayoścāntaramantararvedī /
tadapekṣayā diśā vibhajeta" iti ācāryāḥ /
"tatrāpi mahodayaṃ mūlamavadhīkṛtya" iti yāyāvarīyaḥ /
"aniyatatvāddiśā maniścico digvibhāga" ityeke /
tathā hi yo vāmanasvāminaḥ pūrvaḥ sa brahmaśilāyāḥ paścimaḥ, yo gādhipurasya dakṣiṇaḥ sa kālapriyasyottara iti /
"avadhinibandhanamidaṃ rupamitarattvaniyatameva" iti yāyāvarīyaḥ /
"prācyapācīpratīcyudīcyaḥ catasro diśaḥ" ityeke /

children.translated_text: On that they say —

children.text: "catasṛṣvapi dikṣu raṇe dviṣataḥ prati yena citracaritena /
children.translated_text: "In all four directions, by whom a marvelous deed was performed against the enemy in battle —
unprecedented, without [equal in the] south, without [rival in the] west, and unsurpassed [in the] north."

body.translated_text: "The region between <s>Vinaśana</s> and <s>Prayāga</s>, and between the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and <s>Yamunā</s>, is the <s>Antarvedī</s> (the Doab). With reference to that, one should divide the directions" — say the teachers. "And therein, taking <s>Mahodaya</s> as the center" — says <s>Yāyāvarīya</s>. "Because directions are not fixed, there is no definite division of directions" — say some. For indeed, what is east of <s>Vāmanasvāmin</s> is west of <s>Brahmaśilā</s>; what is south of <s>Gādhipura</s> is north of <s>Kālapriya</s>. "This form [of division] is dependent on a fixed reference point, but the other [absolute form] is indeed fixed" — says <s>Yāyāvarīya</s>. "<s>Prācī</s> (east), <s>Pācī</s> (south), <s>Pratīcī</s> (west), and <s>Udīcī</s> (north) — these are the four directions" — say some.

body.text: "aindrī, āgneyī, yāmyā, nerṛtī, vāruṇī, vāyavyā kauberī, aiśānī cāṣṭauddiśaḥ" ityeke /

children.translated_text: On that they say —

children.text: "ekaṃ jyotirddaśau dve trijagati gaditānyabjajāsyaiścaturbhir bhūtānāṃ pañcamaṃ yānyalamṛtuṣu tathā ṣaṭsu nānāvidhāni /
children.translated_text: "One light, two [eyes] in ten [directions], three worlds spoken by the four mouths of the lotus-born (<s>Brahmā</s>), the fifth of the elements, of various kinds in the six seasons,

children.text: yuṣmākaṃ tāni satpatridaśamuninutānyaṣṭadigbhāñji bhānor yānti prāhne navatvaṃ daśa dadhatu śivaṃ dīdhitānāṃ śatāni" //
children.translated_text: those seven, praised by gods and sages, shining in the eight directions of the sun, attaining nine-fold nature at dawn — may the hundred rays [of the sun] bestow auspiciousness."

body.translated_text: "<s>Aindrī</s> (east), <s>Āgneyī</s> (southeast), <s>Yāmyā</s> (south), <s>Nairṛtī</s> (southwest), <s>Vāruṇī</s> (west), <s>Vāyavyā</s> (northwest), <s>Kauberī</s> (north), and <s>Aiśānī</s> (northeast) — these are the eight directions" — say some.

body.text: "brāhmī nāgīyā ca dve tābhyāṃ saha daśaitāḥ" ityapare /

children.translated_text: On that they say —
"In the narrow confines extending to the borders of the ten directions,
the existence of one with a gross body is difficult in the hamlet of <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s> (the cosmic egg)."

body.translated_text: "<s>Brāhmī</s> (upward) and <s>Nāgīyā</s> (downward) are two [more]; together with them, these are ten" — say others.

body.text:
sarvamastu, vivakṣāparatantrā hi diśāmiyattā /
tatra citrāsvātyantare prācī, tadanusāreṇa pratīcī, ghruveṇodīcī, tadanusāreṇāpācī /
antareṣu vidiśaḥ, ūrdhvaṃ brāhmī, adhaśtānnāgīyeti /
dvividho vyavahāraḥ kavīnāṃ prāksiddho viśiṣṭasthānāvadhisādhyaśca /

children.translated_text: In the previously established [usage], the east —

children.text: "dvitrairvyonmi purāṇamauktikamaṇiccheyaiḥ sthitaṃ tārakair jyotsnāpānabharālasena vapuṣā sutpāścakorāṅganāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Adorned with two or three ancient pearl-gems of stars, with a body languid from the intoxication of drinking moonlight, the <s>cakora</s>-women have fallen asleep;

children.text: yāto 'stācalacūlamudūsamadhucchatracchaviścandramāḥ prācī bālabiḍālalocanarucāṃ jātā ca pātraṃ kakup" //
children.translated_text: the moon has gone to the crest of the western mountain, with the splendor of its honey-like parasol, and the eastern quarter has become a vessel for the gleam of a kitten's eyes."

body.translated_text: Be that as it may, the number of directions depends on the speaker's intention. Among these, [the direction] between <s>Citrā</s> (Spica) and <s>Svāti</s> (Arcturus) is east; correspondingly, west; the pole-star [indicates] north; correspondingly, south. In between are the intermediate directions; upward is <s>Brāhmī</s>; downward is <s>Nāgīyā</s>. The usage of poets is twofold: that which is previously established, and that which is determined by reference to a specific place.

children.translated_text: The south —
"He who was going south, toward the southern direction, shone exceedingly,
like the blessed sun wishing to leave the southern direction."
The west —
"Behold, O one of measured speech, fashioned by the sun hanging at the edge of the western direction,
a long reflection upon the lake — like a bridge-construction of gold."
The north —
"There is in the northern direction, the soul of the gods, the great king of mountains named <s>Himālaya</s>,

children.text: pūrvāparau toyanidhī vigāhya sthitaḥ pṛthivyā iva mānadaṇḍaḥ" //
children.translated_text: plunging into the eastern and western oceans, standing like the measuring rod of the earth."
But in the division of directions determined by reference to a specific place, east and west are as follows —

children.text: "yādāṃsi he carata saṃgatagotratantraṃ pūrveṇa candanagireruta paścimena /
children.translated_text: "O kinsmen, go maintaining your clan-alliance, either to the east of <s>Candanagiri</s> (Sandalwood Mountain) or to the west;

children.text: no cennirantaradharādharasetusūtir ākalpameṣa na viraṃsyati vo viyogaḥ" //
children.translated_text: if the unbroken chain of mountains from mountain to bridge does not [protect you], then until the end of creation this separation of yours will not cease."
South and north, as follows —
"Before <s>Kāñcī</s> in the southern direction, and likewise in the northern direction from the ocean,
<s>Anaṅga</s> (the Bodiless One, i.e., <s>Kāma</s>) dwells happily together with <s>Rati</s>, having made his beautiful bow into an ear-ornament circle."

body.text: uttarādāvapyuttaradigabhidhānaṃ, anuttarādāvapi uttaradigabhidhānam /

children.translated_text: Of those, the first —
"There, to the north of the abodes of <s>Dhanapati</s> (<s>Kubera</s>), is my dwelling, visible from afar by its gateway beautiful as <s>Indra</s>'s rainbow;

children.text: yasyodyāne kṛtakatanayaḥ kāntayā varddhito me hastaprāpyaḥ stabakavinato bālamandāravṛkṣaḥ" //
children.translated_text: in whose garden, nurtured by my beloved, the young <s>Mandāra</s> tree, which I raised from a sapling, bends with clusters of flowers within reach of the hand."

body.translated_text: From the north too [one may use] the designation of the northern direction, and from a non-northern [location] too [one may use] the designation of the northern direction.

children.translated_text: The second —
"On the northern side of the <s>Sahyādri</s> mountains, where the river <s>Godāvarī</s> flows,
that region on this entire earth is delightful."

body.text:
evaṃ digantareṣvapi /
tatra deśaparvatanadyādīnāṃ diśāṃ ca yaḥ kramastaṃ tathaiva nibadhnīyāt /
sādhāraṇāṃ tūbhayatra lokaprasiddhitaśca /
tadūdvarṇaniyamaḥ /
tatra paurastyānāṃ śyāmo varṇāḥ, dākṣiṇātyānāṃ kṛṣṇaḥ, pāścātyānāṃ pāṇḍu, udīcyānāṃ gauraḥ, madhyadeśyānāṃ kṛṣṇaḥ śyāmo gauraśca /

children.translated_text: The dark-blue complexion of easterners —
"Upon the dark-blue limbs of the women of <s>Gauḍa</s>, who steal hearts with a single string-necklace,
<s>Anaṅga</s> (the Bodiless One) dances beautifully, having curved his flowery bow into a circle."

body.translated_text: Thus also for the other directions. In this matter, one should compose [poetry] maintaining the same order of countries, mountains, rivers, etc., and of the directions. Common [features] should be [described] in both ways, according to popular knowledge. Now, the rule regarding the description of complexion: therein, the complexion of easterners is dark-blue (<s>śyāma</s>), of southerners is dark (<s>kṛṣṇa</s>), of westerners is pale (<s>pāṇḍu</s>), of northerners is fair (<s>gaura</s>), and of those from the central region is dark, dark-blue, or fair.

children.translated_text: The dark complexion of southerners —
"This disc-orb of the lord of rays, resembling a ball of molten gold, gradually sinks with dimming light from the sky;

children.text: athaiṣa prācīnaḥ sarati muralīgaṇḍamalinas tarucchāyācakraiḥ stabakita iva dhvāntavisaraḥ //
children.translated_text: and now this mass of darkness, stained like the cheek of a flute, dappled with circles of tree-shadows, spreads from the east like clusters of flowers."
The pale complexion of westerners —
"The bud of the <s>Bakula</s> tree, upon whose honey the bee-women cast their playful, longing glances at the smiling branches, becomes like a lock of hair;

children.text: kiṃ cedānīṃ yavanataruṇīpāṇḍugaṇḍasthalībhyaḥ kāntiḥ stokaṃ racayati padaṃ nāgavallīcchadeṣu //
children.translated_text: and now, from the pale cheeks of <s>Yavana</s> (Greek/Western) maidens, a slight luster makes its mark upon the leaves of the betel vine."
The fair complexion of northerners —

children.text: "puṣpaiḥ samprati kañcanārataravaḥ pratyaṅgamāliṅgitāḥ vā līkīdaśanavraṇāruṇataraiḥ patrairaśoko 'rcitaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Now the golden <s>Āra</s> (brass-tree) trees are embraced limb by limb with flowers, or the <s>Aśoka</s> is worshipped with leaves reddened more by the tooth-marks of <s>Līkī</s> (parrots);
the <s>Campaka</s> too has bloomed, capable of stealing the beauty of northern women, and the <s>Pāṭala</s> tree with its madder-red buds writes yet another inscription."
Or as follows —
"Upon the line-marked limbs of <s>Kāśmīrī</s> women, in their swaying waves of beauty,
it is as if sixteen-quality gold has been melted and applied."
The dark complexion of those from the central region, as follows —
"All beheld <s>Pāñcālī</s> (<s>Draupadī</s>), who was dark (<s>Kṛṣṇā</s>),
like a streak of smoke from the fire of <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>'s wrath, which was the sole destroyer of the <s>Kuru</s> dynasty."

body.text:
tadnmadhyadeśyaśyāmatā /
na ca kavimārge śyāmakṛṣṇayoḥ pāṇḍugaurayorvā mahānviśeṣa iti kavisamayeṣvavocāma /

children.translated_text: The fair complexion of those from the central region —
"Upon your [cheek] fair as a ball of fresh butter, O garland-freed one, reflecting the image of the moon,
the face of the princess of <s>Uttarakosala</s> is reflected, with a mark resembling a musk-leaf pattern."

body.translated_text: That is the dark-blue complexion of those from the central region. And on the path of poets there is no great difference between dark-blue and dark, or between pale and fair — thus we have stated in the poetic conventions.

body.text:
viśeṣastu pūrvadeśe rājaputryādīnā gauraḥ pāṇḍurvā varṇaḥ /
evaṃ dakṣiṇadeśe 'pi /

children.translated_text: Of those, the first —
"Upon the cheek of <s>Jānakī</s> (<s>Sītā</s>), which steals the luster of young elephant tusks, upon her lotus-face with its horripilation of love's smile broadly blooming,

children.text: muhuḥ paśyañchṛṇvanrajanicarasenākalakalaṃ jaṭājūṭagranthiṃ draḍhayati raghūṇāṃ parivṛḍhaḥ" //
children.translated_text: the chief of the <s>Raghu</s> dynasty tightens the knot of his matted locks, repeatedly gazing [at her] while hearing the tumult of the army of the night-wanderers (<s>Rākṣasas</s>)."

body.translated_text: However, the distinction is that in the eastern region, princesses and the like have a fair or pale complexion. Likewise in the southern region also.

children.translated_text: The second —
"Among all those wives of <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), who were all of moon-like radiance,
<s>Rukmiṇī</s> shone in their midst, like the science of grammar among all the sciences."
Thus other [examples] too should be inferred as appropriate —
That which is stated contrary to the stated rule, the learned call a violation of regional convention (<s>deśaviruddha</s>);
that is to be carefully avoided, and illustrations of it are [classified] among the faults.
Thus the division of regions has been outlined for the wise in mere seminal form;
he who desires to know more, let him consult my <s>Bhuvanakośa</s> (Compendium of the World).

body.text: iti rājaśekharakṛtau kāvyamīmāṃsāyāṃ kavirahasye prathame 'dhikaraṇe deśavibhāgaḥ saptadaśo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the seventeenth chapter, on the Division of Regions, in the first section called <s>Kavirahasya</s> (Secrets of the Poet), of the <s>Kāvyamīmāṃsā</s> composed by <s>Rājaśekhara</s>.
Chapter 18

body.text: aṣṭādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ 18
body.translated_text: Eighteenth Chapter — 18

children.translated_text: The Division of Time. Time is differentiated by divisions such as <s>kāṣṭhā</s> (moment) and so forth.

children.text: kāṣṭā nimeṣā daśa pañca triṃśacca kāṣṭhāḥ kathitāḥ kaleti /
children.translated_text: "Ten eye-blinks make one <s>kāṣṭhā</s>, and thirty <s>kāṣṭhās</s> are said to make one <s>kalā</s>;
thirty <s>kalās</s> make one <s>muhūrta</s>, and with thirty [<s>muhūrtas</s>] the night and day are completed."

body.text:
te ca caitraghāśvayujamāsayorbhavataḥ /
caitrātparaṃ pratimāsaṃ mauhūrttikī divasavṛddhiḥ niśāhāniśca trimāsyāḥ, tataḥ paraṃ mauhūrttikī niśāvṛddhiḥ divasahāniśca /
āśvayujītparataḥ punaretadeva viparītam /
rāśaito rāśyantarasaṅkramaṇamuṣṇabhāso māsaḥ, varṣādi dakṣiṇāyanaṃ, śiśirādyuttarāyaṇaṃ, dvayayanaḥ saṃvatsara iti sauraṃ mānam /
pañcadaśāhorātraḥ pakṣaḥ /
varddhamānasomaḥ śuklo, vardhdamānakṛṣṇimā kṛṣṇā iti pitryaṃ māsamānam /
amunā ca vedoditaḥ kṛtsno 'pi kriyākalpaḥ /
pitryameva vyatyayitapakṣaṃ cāndramasam /
idamāryāvarttavāsinaśca kavayaśca mānamāśritāḥ /
evaṃ ca dvau pakṣau māsaḥ /
dvau māsāvṛtuḥ /
ṣaṇṇāmṛtūnāṃ paravarttaḥ saṃvatsaraḥ /
sa ca caitrādiriti daivajñāḥ, śrāvaṇādiriti lokayātrāvidaḥ /
tatra nabhā nabhasyaśca varṣāḥ, īṣa ūrjaśca śarat, sahaḥ sahasyaśca hemantaḥ, tapastasyaśca śiśiraḥ, madhurmādhavaśca vasantaḥ, śukraḥ śuciśca grīṣmaḥ /
tatra "varṣāsu pūrvo vāyuḥ" iti kavayaḥ /
"pāścātyaḥ, paurastyastu pratihantā" ityācāryāḥ /
tadāhuḥ-
"purovātā hatā prāvṛṭ paścādvātā hatā śarat" iti /

children.translated_text: They say —
"In the rainy season, the sky is ceaselessly laden with the full burden of water from the clouds,
and the westerly winds blow, fragrant with the scent of <s>Kadamba</s> flowers."

body.translated_text: These [equal divisions] occur in the months of <s>Caitra</s> and <s>Āśvayuja</s>. From <s>Caitra</s> onward, each month there is a <s>muhūrta</s>'s increase in daytime and decrease in nighttime for three months, and thereafter a <s>muhūrta</s>'s increase in nighttime and decrease in daytime. From <s>Āśvayuja</s> onward, this same [pattern] is reversed. The transit of the hot-rayed one (sun) from one zodiacal sign to the next is a month; from the rains onward is the southern course (<s>dakṣiṇāyana</s>), from winter onward is the northern course (<s>uttarāyaṇa</s>), and two courses make a year — this is the solar reckoning. Fifteen day-nights make a fortnight (<s>pakṣa</s>). The waxing moon is the bright [fortnight] (<s>śukla</s>), the increasing darkness is the dark [fortnight] (<s>kṛṣṇa</s>) — this is the ancestral (<s>pitrya</s>) monthly reckoning. By this reckoning the entire ritual calendar prescribed by the <s>Vedas</s> [is governed]. The ancestral reckoning with reversed fortnights is the lunar reckoning. The poets and inhabitants of <s>Āryāvarta</s> follow this system. Thus two fortnights make a month, two months make a season (<s>ṛtu</s>), and the cycle of six seasons makes a year. The astrologers say it begins with <s>Caitra</s>, while those versed in worldly affairs say it begins with <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>. Therein, <s>Nabha</s> and <s>Nabhasya</s> are the rains; <s>Īṣa</s> and <s>Ūrja</s> are autumn; <s>Saha</s> and <s>Sahasya</s> are the cold season (<s>hemanta</s>); <s>Tapas</s> and <s>Tapasya</s> are the dewy season (<s>śiśira</s>); <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Mādhava</s> are spring; <s>Śukra</s> and <s>Śuci</s> are summer. Therein, "in the rains the first wind [comes from the east]" — say the poets. "[It comes] from the west, while the eastern [wind] is the opposing one" — say the teachers. They state —  "When the wind blows from the front, the rains are destroyed; when the wind blows from behind, autumn is destroyed."

body.text: "vastuvṛttaratantraṃ, kavisamayaḥ pramāṇam" iti yāyāvarīyaḥ /

children.translated_text: They say —

children.text: "paurastyastoyadarttoḥ pavana iva patanpāvakasyeva dhūmo viśvasyevādisargaḥ praṇava iva paraṃ pāvanaṃ vedarāśeḥ /
children.translated_text: "Like the wind from the eastern cloud-season, like the smoke of fire, like the first creation of the universe, like the <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ) — the supreme purifier of the mass of <s>Vedas</s>,

children.text: sandhyānṛttotsavocchoriva madanariponandināndīninādaḥ sorasyāgre sukhaṃ vo vitaratu vinatānandanaḥ syandanasya" //
children.translated_text: like the rising sound at the festival of the twilight dance of the enemy of <s>Madana</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) — may the son of <s>Vinatā</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>), [who stands] before his (<s>Viṣṇu</s>'s) chariot, bestow happiness upon you."

body.translated_text: "Actual occurrence is the basis; poetic convention is the authority" — says <s>Yāyāvarīya</s>.

children.translated_text: In autumn, the wind is not fixed to any direction, as follows —
"In the mornings blew the breezes that carried dark dewdrops,
fragrant with the astringent scent of the buds and calyxes of <s>Śephālikā</s> (night-jasmine)."

body.text:
"hemante pāścātyo vāyuḥ", iti eke /
"udīcya" iti apare /
"ubhayamapi"iti yāyāvarīyaḥ /

children.translated_text: Of those, the western —

"Breaking the rows of trees withered by frost, rising from the slopes of the snowy mountains, rough and bark-stripping, shaking the <s>Cātaka</s> birds startled by the mass of thick waves of the <s>Rambhā</s> (plantain) waters,
the western wind blows with force, showering a rain of hailstone spray — a breeze dense as if trampled by elephants, dripping with resin, carrying the calls of <s>Sārasa</s> cranes."

body.translated_text: "In winter the wind is from the west" — say some. "From the north" — say others. "Both" — says <s>Yāyāvarīya</s>.

children.translated_text: The northern —
"Scattering the hair-ornaments of young women, making their fur garments flutter, kissing the waters of the <s>Candrabhāgā</s> river, singularly fierce with birch-bark,

children.text: ete kastūrikaiṇapraṇayasurabhayo vallabhā bāhlavīnāṃ kaulūtīkelikārāḥ paricayitahimaṃ vāyavo vāntyudīcyāḥ" //
children.translated_text: these northerly winds blow — beloved of the women of <s>Bāhlava</s> (Balkh), fragrant with the love-scent of musk deer, playmates for the sports of <s>Kaulūta</s> (Kullu) women, bearing the touch of frost."

body.text:
śiśire 'pi hemantavadudīcyaḥ pāścātyo vā /
vasante dakṣiṇaḥ /

children.translated_text: That is stated —

"Shaking the rows of <s>Alaṅkāvana</s> groves, repeatedly making the <s>Alaka</s> vine-tendrils of <s>Kerala</s> women dance, instantly loosening the hair-knots of <s>Āndhra</s> women, waving the betel vines,

children.text: uddāmaṃ dākṣiṇātyo malitamalayajaḥ sārithirmīnaketoḥ prātpaḥ sīmantinīnāṃ madhusamayasuhṛnmānacauraḥ samīraḥ" //
children.translated_text: the unbridled southern wind, anointed with sandal paste from the <s>Malaya</s> mountains, the charioteer of the Fish-bannered one (<s>Kāma</s>), the friend of beautiful women in the spring season, the thief of their pride, blows in the early morning."

body.translated_text: In the dewy season (<s>śiśira</s>) too, the wind is from the north or west, as in winter. In spring, it is from the south.

body.text:
"ubhayatadikko vāyurgrīṣme" ityeke /
"naiṛrtaḥ " ityapare /
"ubhayamapi" iti yāyāvarīyaḥ /

children.translated_text: Of those, the first —
"Thick pillars of dust, whose whirlwind-circles kiss the vault of the sky, weave the heavens with the semblance of columns for the coming cloud-canopy;

children.text: kiṃ cānyanmṛgatṛṣṇiṅkāmbuvasaraiḥ pātrāṇi vītārṇasāṃ sindhūnāmiha sūtrayanti divaseṣvāgāminīṃ sampadam" //
children.translated_text: moreover, with the water-flows of mirages, they string together the vessels of the waterless rivers, heralding the coming abundance of rainy days."

body.translated_text: "The wind blows from both directions in summer" — say some. "From the southwest (<s>Nairṛta</s>)" — say others. "Both" — says <s>Yāyāvarīya</s>.

children.translated_text: The second —
"This sun burns with rays as if made of fire, the entire earth is as if laden with heaps of embers,

children.text: vāyuḥ kukūlamiva varṣati naiṛrtaśca kārśānavairiva śarairmadanaśca hanti" //
children.translated_text: the southwestern (<s>Nairṛta</s>) wind showers as if [raining] chaff, and <s>Madana</s> (<s>Kāma</s>) strikes with arrows as if of conflagration."
Furthermore —
Depositing embryos in the <s>Balākā</s> cranes, producing the shoots of bamboo with their spontaneous sounds,
"sealing the dust, the clouds in the rainy season obstruct the military campaigns of kings."
Bearing the flowers of <s>Sallakī</s>, <s>Sāla</s>, <s>Śilīndhra</s> (mushroom), and <s>Yūthī</s> (jasmine), with blooming <s>Lāṅgalīka</s> (a plant),
beautiful with the fragrance of the scorched earth — this is the harbinger of the rain-clouds.
The forests are dark-green with the leaves of indigo plants, the mountains glisten washed by streams of rain,
the rivers have their banks broken by the flood-waters, and the grassy meadows are thick with <s>Indragopa</s> (red velvet mites).
Delighting the <s>Cakora</s> birds, stealing the conduct of ascetics, [a time] when separated women gaze upon the road of their lord,
when caravans of travelers set out for home — this is the season with a sky inflated by rain-clouds.
The pleasure-excursions of amorous she-elephants, the reclining on couches atop lofty mansions,
and the enjoyment of the four-fold [pleasures] with musk-scented [unguents] — she (the rainy season) is the first hostess of the cloud-season.
With restless, fluttering <s>Cātaka</s> birds, with the rise of color in the deer (<s>Kuraṅga</s>), with the swelling sound of frogs, with serpents proud and bold with intoxication,

children.text: śikhaṇḍikulatāṇḍavāmuditamadgukaṅkāhvayo viyogiṣu ghanāgamaḥ smaraviṣaṃ viṣaṃ muñcati //
children.translated_text: with the dance of the peacock-family delighting <s>Madgu</s>, <s>Kaṅka</s>, and <s>Āhvaya</s> (water-birds) — the arrival of the clouds releases poison upon poison for those who are separated [from their beloved].
With bursting <s>Kuṭaja</s> buds, with profusions of blooming <s>Nīpa</s> flowers, a companion of <s>Dhava</s> blossoms, with clusters of <s>Arjuna</s> flowers gathered,

children.text: kadambakaluṣāmbaraḥ kalitaketakīkorakaś calanniculasañcayo harati hanta dharmātyayaḥ //
children.translated_text: with the sky clouded by <s>Kadamba</s> [pollen], with the forming of <s>Ketakī</s> buds, with the moving mass of low clouds — alas, the passing of <s>Dharma</s> (moral restraint) enchants [all]!

body.text: varṣāḥ //
body.translated_text: The Rains.

children.translated_text: Quickly silencing the proud peacocks with her thundering, emboldening the <s>Kurara</s> (osprey) birds and bees,
Autumn approaches, causing the lotuses to bloom and opening the <s>Kumuda</s> (white water-lily) and <s>Utpala</s> (blue lotus).
She shines, bestowing flowers upon <s>Bandhūka</s>, <s>Bāṇāsana</s> (Indian cane), <s>Kuṅkuma</s> (saffron),
<s>Śephālikā</s> (night-jasmine), <s>Satpapalāśa</s>, <s>Kāśa</s> (reed-grass), <s>Maṇḍīra</s>, <s>Saugandhika</s> (fragrant water-lily), and <s>Mālatī</s> (jasmine).

children.text: sakhañjarīṭā sapayaḥ prasādā sā kasya no mānasamācchinati /
children.translated_text: Accompanied by <s>Khañjarīṭa</s> (wagtail) birds and the clarity of waters, whose mind does she not captivate?
Followed by flocks of <s>Kādamba</s> (geese), <s>Kāraṇḍava</s> (a type of duck), <s>Cakravāka</s> (ruddy shelduck), <s>Sārasa</s> (crane), and <s>Krauñca</s> (curlew) birds.
Bringing flocks of <s>Kalahaṃsa</s> (swans), purifying the waters by the sight of <s>Agastya</s> (the star Canopus),

children.text: muktāsu śubhraṃ dadhatī ca garbhaṃ śaradvacitraiścaritaiścakāsti //
children.translated_text: and placing a white embryo in the pearls — Autumn shines with [her] varied deeds.

children.text: kṣitiṃ khananto vṛṣabhāḥ khurāgrai rodho viṣāṇairdviradā radantaḥ /
children.translated_text: Bulls ploughing the earth with the tips of their hooves, elephants uprooting the banks with their tusks,

children.text: śṛṅgaṃ tyajanto ruravaśca jīrṇaṃ kurvanti lokānavalokanotkān //
children.translated_text: and <s>Ruru</s> deer shedding their old antlers — [all] make the people eager to behold [them].
Here the sky all around has brilliantly white moonlight-water and a dark-blue radiance,
the <s>Surebhavīthī</s> (the Milky Way) is a stairway to heaven, and the worn cloud-fragments are pale white.
On the great <s>Navamī</s> (ninth day), there is worship of all weapons, and <s>Nīrājana</s> (lustration ceremony) of horses, warriors, and elephants;
on <s>Dīpālikā</s> (<s>Dīvālī</s>), various festivities are to be performed here by kings preparing for military campaigns.
In the sky, a splendid multitude of brilliant stars; the earth is fit for the movement of chariots;

children.text: bhāskaraḥ śaradi dīpradīdhitirbudhyate ca saha mādhavaḥ suraiḥ //
children.translated_text: in autumn the sun has radiant rays, and <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) awakens together with the gods.

children.text: kedāra eva kalamāḥ pariṇāmanabhrāḥ prācīnamāmalakamardhati pākanīlam /
children.translated_text: In the paddy fields themselves, the rice shoots have clouds of ripening; the ancient <s>āmalaka</s> (gooseberry) grows dark-blue with ripening,
the <s>ervāruka</s> (cucumber), bursting open, releases its inner fragrance, and the old <s>trapusī</s> (gourd) fruits turn sour.
In the courtyards of the houses of farmers, made lovely by the fragrance of newly threshed rice grains falling,
the young wives delight [all], with their bangles slipping from their hands shaken by the vigorous wielding of pestles.

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ ravistapati nīca ivācirāḍhyaḥ śṛṅgaṃ rurustyajati mitramivākṛtajñaḥ /
children.translated_text: The sun blazes fiercely, like a low person who has recently gained wealth; the <s>ruru</s> deer sheds its horns, like an ungrateful man [abandoning] a friend;

children.text: toyaṃ prasīdati muneriva dharmacintā kāmī daridra iva śoṣamupauti paṅkam //
children.translated_text: the water becomes clear, like a sage's contemplation of <s>dharma</s>; the mud dries up like a lover become destitute.
The rivers flow with oyster shells carried along in winding courses, with turtles rising from the bellies of sandbanks marked with single lines,
and in this [season] the cranes follow the fish fleeing through the thin rippling waters, offering their fearsome catches.
With banks free from mud, gleaming with the shining scales of <s>śaphara</s> fish, with baby fish darting about in confusion as the swooping <s>kurara</s> (osprey) terrifies them,
with turtles rolling on the sandbanks, and bustling with the chatter of restless herons — the accumulated river water, dense in autumn, subsides.

body.text: śarat //
body.translated_text: <s>Śarat</s> (Autumn).

children.translated_text: With two or three <s>mucukunda</s> buds on the <s>lavalī</s> vines, with three or four flower-buds gradually [appearing],
with five or six <s>phalinī</s> blossoms — the new advent of the <s>himartu</s> (winter season) triumphs!
Adorned with <s>punnāga</s> and <s>rodhra</s> blossoms as ear-ornaments, the lovely-browed women, their bodies curved within tight bodices,
bear their braids marked with streaks of obliquely gleaming <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron) and beeswax, anointed with fragrant oils.
The more the cold season blooms forth, with winds scattering heaps of frost-powder,

children.text: tathā tathā yauvanaśālinīnāṃ kavoṣṇatāmatra kucā labhante //
children.translated_text: the more do the breasts of women endowed with youth acquire a pleasant warmth.
Here there are choice boar-meats, fresh rice dishes, curds thickened with grains of mustard,

children.text: sukomalāḥ sarṣapakandalīśca bhuktvā jano nindati vaidyavidyām //
children.translated_text: and tender stalks of mustard greens — having eaten these, the people scorn the science of medicine!
Here the remedy is with lukewarm waters; here any food or drink whatsoever tastes delicious;

children.text: sudurbhagāmatra nipīḍya śete svastyastu nityaṃ tuhinarttave 'smai //
children.translated_text: here the unfortunate one lies pressing [against the cold] — may there always be well-being in this frost season!

children.text: vimuktabarhā vimadā mayūrāḥ praruḍhagodhūmayavā ca sīmā /
children.translated_text: Peacocks who have shed their tail-feathers, free from rut; fields where wheat and barley have sprouted;
the birth of tiger cubs; water mixed with mist — these signs of <s>hemanta</s> (early winter) prevail!
And here the fields triumph with ripening <s>śamī</s> grain-crops;
the nights have <s>triśaṅku</s> and <s>tilaka</s> [stars visible], and salt is being prepared.
In gardens, the male <s>kokila</s> (cuckoo) falls silent; on the faces of the bee-women, the seal of silence [is set];
the flight of birds through the sky becomes sluggish in <s>hemanta</s> (early winter), and the pride of serpents is destroyed.
The ripening of <s>karkandhū</s> (jujube) fruits and <s>nāraṅgī</s> (orange) fruits is in excess; <s>khāṇḍava</s> (a sweet preparation) also appears;

children.text: kṛṣṇekṣūṇāṃ puṇḍrakāṇāṃ ca garbhe mādhuryaśrīrjāyate kāpyapūrvā //
children.translated_text: and in the core of dark sugarcanes and <s>puṇḍra</s> (white sugarcane), an unprecedented glory of sweetness is born.

children.text: yeṣāṃ madhyemandiraṃ talpasampat pārśve dārāḥ sphāratāruṇyatārāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those whose house is in the center, whose bedding is excellent, whose wives at their side are stars radiant with ample youth,
whose playful fire conceals its abundant smoke — they know <s>hemanta</s> (early winter) as if it were the remainder of <s>grīṣma</s> (summer).

body.text:
iti hemantaḥ /
hemantadharmaḥ śiśiraḥ, viśeṣastu /

children.translated_text: 'The night is long, with its watches suited for lovemaking at the peak of passion; the fierce wind carries the fragrance of <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron) paste;
