the bed-furnishing is of double-layered cotton quilts — what more? — and here dense fumes of <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood) incense are valued.

children.text: ba" āśleṣiṇā pṛthurataklamapītaśītam āyāminīṃ ghanamudo rajanīṃ yuvānaḥ /
children.translated_text: The young men, embracing [their beloveds], having drunk away the cold during the long and cloud-delighting night,
sleep with cotton quilts wrapped around their feet, their toes curling at the loosening of the waist-knot from the repeated movements of their thighs.

body.translated_text: Thus ends <s>hemanta</s> (early winter). <s>Śiśira</s> (late winter) shares the characteristics of <s>hemanta</s>; the distinction, however, is:

children.text: pāne 'mbhasoḥ surasanīrasayorna bhāti sparśakriyāsu tuhinānalayorna cātra /
children.translated_text: In the drinking of waters, there is no beauty as between <s>surā</s> (wine) and sugarcane juice; nor in the sense of touch between frost and fire;

children.text: no durbhagāsubhagayoḥ parirambhaṇe ca no sevane ca śaśibhāskarayorviśeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: nor in the embrace between the unfortunate and the fortunate; nor in the attendance upon the moon and the sun is there distinction [in this season].

children.text: puṣpakriyā marubake jalakelinindā kundānyaśeṣakusumeṣu dhuri sthitāni /
children.translated_text: The use of flowers is [limited to] the <s>marubaka</s> and water-sports are scorned; <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) blossoms stand foremost among all flowers;

children.text: saubhāgyameṇatilakādbhajate 'rkabimbaṃ kāle tuṣāriṇi dahanti ca candanāni //
children.translated_text: the sun's disc claims the beauty of the <s>mṛga-tilaka</s> (musk-deer mark); and in the season of frost, sandalwood pastes burn [the skin].
On the <s>siddhārtha</s> (white mustard) stalks, progressively diminishing in succession, with their dense rows of needle-like pods split open,
with only two or three flowers remaining, the process of ripening gradually assumes a tawny hue.
In the pleasure-ponds, struck by the fierce northern wind, with fish submerged at the bottom of the water,
with only the lotus stalks remaining of the lotus creepers — the eye no longer finds delight.
An intoxicated elephant, a spotted deer finding contentment, a flower-eating boar, a <s>lulāya</s> bird of steadfast courage,

children.text: daridranindyaḥ sadhanaikavandyaḥ sa eṣa kālaḥ śiśiraḥ karālaḥ //
children.translated_text: condemned by the poor, praised by the wealthy alone — such is this terrible season of <s>śiśira</s> (late winter)!
Sweet only as a new bride's untried anger, with fire of cow-dung cakes as sole warmth, cruel with frost-laden winds that are [harsh as] the embrace of strangers,

children.text: galitavibhavasyajñevādya dyutirmasṛṇā rave rvirahivanitāvaktraupabhyaṃ bibharttiṃ niśākaraḥ //
children.translated_text: the sun's lustre is faint like that of one whose wealth has declined — and the moon bears on its face the semblance of a woman separated [from her lover].
Women, naturally of <s>pitta</s> (bilious) constitution, with <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron) paste smeared upon their hips, breasts, arms, thighs, and feet,
here, in the bloom of fresh youth, clasped throughout the entire night, steal away the fever-like torment of <s>śiśira</s> (late winter) from the very earth itself.

body.text: śiśiraḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Śiśira</s> (Late Winter).

children.translated_text: 'In <s>Caitra</s> (March-April), the intoxication intensifies for parrots and <s>sārikā</s> (mynas), for <s>hārīta</s> birds, <s>dātyūha</s> (gallinules), and bees,

children.text: puṃskokilānāṃ sahakārabandhuḥ madasya kālaḥ purareṣu eva //
children.translated_text: and for male <s>kokilas</s> (cuckoos), friends of the mango tree — the time of passion arrives precisely in the spring season.'

children.text: mano 'dhikaṃ cātra vilāsalāsye preṅkhāsu dolāsu ca sundarīṇāṃ /
children.translated_text: And here, the minds [of women turn] ever more to playful grace, to swings and cradles of beautiful women,

children.text: gīte ca gaurīcaritāvataṃse pūjāprapañce ca manobhavasya //
children.translated_text: to songs adorned with the exploits of <s>Gaurī</s>, and to the elaborate worship of <s>Manobhava</s> (the god of love).

children.text: puṃskokilaḥ kūjati pañcamena balādvilāsā yuvatau sphuranti /
children.translated_text: The male <s>kokila</s> (cuckoo) sings in the fifth note (<s>pañcama</s>); amorous gestures spontaneously arise in young women;

children.text: smaro vasante 'tra navaiḥ prasūnaiḥ svacāpayaṣṭerghaṭanāṃ karoti //
children.translated_text: <s>Smara</s> (the god of love) in spring fashions the stringing of his bow with fresh blossoms.
For the devoted wives whose beloved has been seized by passion, clad in garments of deep crimson,

children.text: smarīkṛte preyasi bhaktibhājāṃ viśeṣaveṣaḥ svadate vadhūnām //
children.translated_text: with <s>sindūra</s> (vermilion) adorning the parting of their hair, a special attire is pleasing in spring.
This is the time when the <s>karṇikāra</s> tree is exuberant with blossoms, when the <s>kāñcanāra</s> (golden tree) is worshipped by the <s>pañcārcita</s> flowers,
when the <s>kovidāra</s> is skilled in blooming forth, and the <s>sinduvāra</s> (vitex) is ready to blossom.
<s>Rohītaka</s>, <s>āmrātaka</s>, <s>kiṅkirāta</s>, <s>madhūka</s>, and <s>mocā</s> (plantain), along with <s>mādhavī</s> creepers,
triumph in spring — and the <s>śobhāñjana</s> (drumstick tree) and the <s>kesara</s> (filament-bearing tree), laden with masses of flowers!

children.text: yo mādhavīmukuladṛṣṭiṣu veṇibandho yaḥ kokilakalaruteḥ kathane ca lābhaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who is the braid-binding for the glances that are <s>mādhavī</s> buds, who is the gain in the narration of the <s>kokila's</s> melodious song,

children.text: pūjāvidhirdamanakena ca yaḥ smarasya tasminmadhuḥ sa bhagavāngururaṅganānām //
children.translated_text: who is the ritual of worship of <s>Smara</s> (the god of love) with <s>damanaka</s> flowers — that blessed <s>Madhu</s> (Spring) is the master of women!

children.text: nāliṅgitaḥ kurabakastalako na dṛṣṭo nā tāḍitaśca caraṇaiḥ sudṛśāmaśokaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>kurabaka</s> has not been embraced, the <s>tilaka</s> has not been gazed upon, the <s>aśoka</s> has not been struck by the feet of beautiful women,

children.text: siktā na vaktramadhunā bakulaśca caitre citraṃ tathāpi bhavati prasavāvakīrṇāḥ //
children.translated_text: nor has the <s>bakula</s> been sprinkled with mouth-wine in <s>Caitra</s> — and yet, wondrously, they become covered with blossoms!
In <s>Caitra</s>, the <s>aśoka</s> trees are remarkable — red and blue; the golden <s>aśoka</s> is the third, yellow in color;
the victorious power among those flower-varieties of the flower-born god (<s>Kāma</s>) extends even over the three worlds — <s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, and <s>Svaḥ</s>.
For <s>gūvāka</s> (areca nut) trees, <s>nālikera</s> (coconut) palms, <s>hintāla</s> palms, <s>pāṭala</s> and <s>kiṃśuka</s> (flame-of-the-forest) trees,
for <s>kharjūra</s> (date) palms and <s>tāḍa-tāḍī</s> (palmyra) trees — spring is the cause of bestowing garlands of flowers.
Causing the blossoming of fresh <s>mallikā</s> (jasmine), charming with the petals of <s>śirīṣa</s> (silk-cotton) blossoms,
bestowing flowers upon the golden <s>ketakī</s> (screw-pine) — this is <s>grīṣma</s> (summer), which makes the <s>dhātakī</s> (fire-flame bush) bloom!
With the fruits of date-palms, <s>jambū</s> (rose-apple), <s>panasa</s> (jackfruit), mango, <s>mocā</s> (plantain), <s>priyāla</s>, <s>pūgī</s> (areca), and <s>nālikera</s> (coconut),
couples, overcoming the languor of fatigue, devote themselves here to the pursuit of love.
Streams, wells, and cisterns; rest-houses full of travelers on scorching days;

children.text: śucau samabhyarthitasaktupāne prage ca sāyaṃ ca vahanti mārgāḥ //
children.translated_text: in the hot season, roads carry [people seeking] <s>saktu</s> (barley-drink) both at dawn and at dusk.
That in which there is sleep during half the day as days are endured, in which water-sports [take place] at the close of day,
in which lovemaking descends in the last watch of the night — that regimen of concentrated effort conquers the dense heat.
The moonlight, delightful as sandalwood paste; the garland of breezes through lattice-windows;
the shower of water-drops from palm-leaf fans — she offers a water-oblation to the hot season.
Camphor powder, mango preparations, <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel leaf) prepared with fresh areca nut,
pearl necklaces, fine thin garments — this is the great secret of the cooling regimen.
Pearl strings smeared with sandalwood paste, lotus-stalk garlands kept moist with water,

children.text: strajaśca maulau smitacampakānāṃ grīṣme 'pi so 'yaṃ śiśirāvatāraḥ" //
children.translated_text: and garlands of gently smiling <s>campaka</s> flowers on the head — even in summer, this is an advent of coolness.
Moreover here —
'The creatures seem as if being cooked; the dust seems as if being heated;

children.text: kkathyanta iva toyāni dhmāyanta iva cādrayaḥ //
children.translated_text: the waters seem as if being boiled; and the mountains seem as if smoking.'

children.text: eṇāḥ sthalīṣu mṛgatṛṣṇikayā hriyante srotastanutvajanitā jalaveṇibandhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Deer on the plains are deceived by mirages; streams form thin braids of water born from their own slenderness;

children.text: tāmyattimīni ca sarāṃsi jalasya śeṣād uccāraghaṭṭighaṭikāvalayāśca kūpāḥ //
children.translated_text: the lakes have their fish languishing from the remaining water, and the wells are [reduced to] chains of bucket-pulleys for drawing [water].

children.text: karabhāḥ śarabhāḥ sarāsabhā madamāyānti bhajanti vikriyām /
children.translated_text: Young camels, <s>śarabha</s> (eight-legged beasts), and wild donkeys grow intoxicated and undergo transformation;
they climb upon the dry lands where <s>karavīra</s> (oleander) and <s>karīra</s> (caper) bushes are in bloom, and rest there.
<s>Rasālā</s> (drink) flavored with mango juice, fruit beverages, <s>mantha</s> (churned drinks) with water as the main ingredient,

children.text: mṛgalāvarasāḥ śṛtaṃ ca dugdha smarasañjīvanamauṣadhaṃ nidādhe //
children.translated_text: the juices of deer and quail, and boiled milk — these are the life-restoring medicines of love in the summer heat.
Women, lovely with water, sandal paste, and beautiful garments of youth, moist with water, wearing necklaces of pearls,
reclining on beds fashioned of plantain leaves, invite <s>Smara</s> (the god of love) and seat him at their side.

children.text: grīṣme cīrīnādavanto vanāntāḥ paṅkābhyaktāḥ sauribhāḥ sebhakolāḥ /
children.translated_text: In summer, the forest edges resound with the cry of crickets; water-buffaloes and <s>sauribha</s> beasts are smeared with mud;
serpents and <s>sāraṅga</s> (deer) herds have flickering tongues; and the trees [droop] with their branch-tips wilted at the roots.

children.text: harmyaṃ ramyaṃ candrikādhautapṛṣṭaṃ kāntocchiṣṭā vāruṇī vārimiśrā /
children.translated_text: A lovely mansion with its roof washed by moonlight; leftover <s>vāruṇī</s> (wine) from the beloved, mixed with water;

children.text: mālāḥ kaṇṭhe pāṭalā mallikānāṃ sadyo grīṣmaṃ hanta hemantayanti //
children.translated_text: rosy garlands of <s>mallikā</s> (jasmine) around the neck — alas, they instantly turn summer into winter!

body.text: grīṣmaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Grīṣma</s> (Summer).

body.text:
caturavasthaśca ṛturupanibandhanīyaḥ /
tadyathā sandhiḥ, śaiśavaṃ, prauḍhiḥ, anavṛttiśca /
ṛtudvayamadhyaṃ sandhiḥ /

children.translated_text: The juncture of <s>śiśira</s> (late winter) and <s>vasanta</s> (spring) is as follows —

children.text: "tyutasumanasaḥ kundāḥ puṣpodgameṣvalasā drumā manasi ca giraṃ gṛhṇantīme giranti na kokilāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) plants have shed their flowers; the trees are sluggish in putting forth blossoms; and these <s>kokilas</s> (cuckoos), though taking up the song in their minds, do not yet sing;

children.text: atha ca savituḥ śītollāsaṃ lunanti marīcayo na ca jaraṭhatāmālambante klamodayadāyinīm" //
children.translated_text: and yet the sun's rays are cutting through the delight of the cold, and they are not yet assuming that staleness which brings weariness.'

body.translated_text: A season should be described in four stages, namely: <s>sandhi</s> (juncture), <s>śaiśava</s> (infancy), <s>prauḍhi</s> (maturity), and <s>anāvṛtti</s> (departure). The interval between two seasons is the <s>sandhi</s> (juncture).

children.translated_text: The infancy of spring (<s>vasanta-śaiśava</s>) —

children.text: "garbhagranthiṣu vīrudhāṃ sumanaso madhye 'ṅkuraṃ pallavā vāñchāmātraparigrahaḥ pikavadhūkaṇṭhodare pañcamaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Among the plants, the flowers are [still] in embryonic knots, the sprouts are midway to becoming leaves, the fifth note (<s>pañcama</s>) has only entered as far as mere desire in the throat of the female <s>kokila</s> (cuckoo);

children.text: kiṃ ca trīṇi jaganti jiṣṇu divasairdvighatrairmanojanmano devasyāpi cirojbhphitaṃ yadi bhavedabhyāsavaśyaṃ dhanuḥ" //
children.translated_text: moreover, [though] the three worlds are to be conquered in just a few days by the god <s>Manmatha</s> (Love), his bow, if it has been long since it was strung, must [first] be brought under control through practice.'
The maturity of spring (<s>vasanta-prauḍhi</s>) —

children.text: "sāmyaṃ samprati sevate vicakilaṃ ṣāṇmāsikairmauktikaiḥ kāntiṃ karṣati kāñcanārakusumaṃ mājjiṣṭadhautātpaṭāt /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>vicakila</s> flower now rivals six-month-old pearls in equality; the <s>kāñcanāra</s> (golden tree) blossom steals its radiance from a madder-washed silk cloth;

children.text: hūṇīnāṃ kurute madhūkamukulaṃ lāvaṇyaluṇṭākatāṃ lāṭīnābhinibhaṃ cakāsti ca patadvṛntāgrataḥ kesaram" //
children.translated_text: the <s>madhūka</s> bud creates a plundering of beauty surpassing <s>Hūṇī</s> women; and the <s>kesara</s> (filament), falling from its stalk-tip, gleams like [the beauty of] <s>Lāṭī</s> women.'
When the signs of a past season continue through flowers and such [into the next season],
that is called the 'continuation of seasonal signs' (<s>liṅgānuvṛtti</s>), and it should be recognized from the world of poetry.
In the rainy season, the continuation of the summer-sign is the blooming of lotuses.

children.text: khaṃ vaste kalaviṅkakaṇṭhamalinaṃ kādambinīkambalaṃ carcā pārayatīva dardurakulaṃ kolāhalairunmadam /
children.translated_text: 'The sky wears a cloak of clouds, dark as the throat of the <s>kalaviṅka</s> (sparrow); the chorus of frogs seems to be completing a wild frenzy of ecstatic chanting;

children.text: gandhaṃ muñcati siktalājasadṛśaṃ varṣeṇa dagdhā sthalī durlakṣyo 'pi vibhāvyate kamalinīhāsena bhāsāṃ patiḥ //
children.translated_text: the parched earth releases a fragrance like dampened <s>lāja</s> (parched grain); and the lord of luminaries (the sun), though hard to discern, is revealed by the smile of the lotus pond.'

body.text: " evamanyā api /

children.translated_text: Furthermore —
The <s>kadamba</s> [flower] that blooms in the summer season is known in the world as <s>dhūlī-kadamba</s> (dust-kadamba);
that very same, at the arrival of the rainy season, becomes <s>dhārā-kadamba</s> (rain-stream-kadamba).

body.translated_text: Similarly for others also.

children.translated_text: For example —
'O blue-throated <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s> (peacock)! When the face of the sky is made grey by clouds of dust, when it is adorned with a rainbow like the bow of a divine archer,
when the lightning flashes weapons and the thunderbolt is hurled — do you not long for the arrival of the battle-clouds of the rainy season?'
The species [of flower] that is born in the rainy season and is called <s>kardamī</s>,
that very same, in autumn, becomes a great festival-flower, fragrant and attended by bees.
For example —
'The lattice-work of creepers, whose great bud-knots have burst open with drops of heavy dew glistening [upon them], whose aged fragrance overflows, has bloomed forth in full —

children.text: nānāhaṃsopadhānaṃ sapadi jalanidheśvotsasarpāparasya jyotsnāśuklopadhānaṃ śayanamiva śaśī nāgabhogāṅkamabhbhaḥ" //
children.translated_text: with various swans as pillows, of the ocean that had just surged up from the other side, the moon, with moonlight-white bedding, [rests] as if on a bed, on the coils of the serpent, radiant —'

body.text: stokānuvṛttiṃ ketakyā api kecidicchanti /

children.translated_text: As [illustrated by]:
'The autumn season was indicated by the days arriving anew,
with feet dusty-grey from <s>ketakī</s> pollen and copper-hued like lotuses.'

body.translated_text: Some wish for a slight continuation of the <s>ketakī</s> (screw-pine) [even into autumn].

children.translated_text: The continuation here is of the signs of autumn — of bows together with <s>kuruṇṭaka</s> flowers;

children.text: hemantavaktre yadi dṛśyate 'pi na dṛśyate bandhavidhiḥ kavīnām //
children.translated_text: even if [something] of the winter season is seen in the face of <s>hemanta</s> (early winter), the method of composition of poets is not thereby seen.

body.text: hemantaśiśirayoraikye sarvaliṅgānuvṛttireva /

children.translated_text: And it is said:
'Twelve months make a year; five seasons, when <s>hemanta</s> and <s>śiśira</s> are combined.'
Spring (<s>surabhi</s>) should be composed with the signs of <s>marubaka</s>, <s>damanaka</s>, <s>punnāga</s>, and their flowers,
and with some [composed] with the continuation of <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) and with variegated beauty.

body.translated_text: In the unity of <s>hemanta</s> (early winter) and <s>śiśira</s> (late winter), [there is] a continuation of all the signs [of both].

children.text: "gṛhe vāhīkayūnāṃ vahati damanako mañjarīkarṇapūrān unmādaḥ pāmarīṇāṃ maruti marubakāmodini vyaktimeti /
children.translated_text: 'In the houses of <s>Vāhīka</s> youths, the <s>damanaka</s> bears clusters as ear-ornaments; the intoxication of <s>pāmarī</s> women becomes manifest when the wind is fragrant with <s>marubaka</s>;

children.text: sadyo bhaṅgānusārastrutasarabhiśirāśīkaraḥ sāhakāraḥ sarparannambhaḥśarāve racayati ca raso racakīcandrakāṇi //
children.translated_text: the mango tree, whose sprinkle of drops [comes] from its instantly breaking sap-laden branches, creates moon-marks of <s>racakī</s> in the water-vessel.

children.text: kunde mandastamāle mukulini vikalaḥ kātaraḥ kiṅkirāte raktāśoke saśokaściramativikace campake kuñcitākṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The traveler is distressed at the <s>kunda</s> (jasmine), languid at the <s>tamāla</s> when it buds, weak and anxious at the <s>kiṅkirāta</s>, sorrowful and red-eyed at the <s>aśoka</s> when it blooms, squinting at the <s>campaka</s>,

children.text: pānthaḥ khedālaso 'pi śravaṇakaṭuraṭaccakramabhyeti dhunvan sotkaṇṭhaḥ ṣaṭpadānāṃ navamadhupaṭalīlampaṭaṃ karpaṭena" //
children.translated_text: even weary with fatigue, the wayfarer goes about shaking off with his garment the swarm of new bees, lustful for fresh honey, buzzing harshly in his ears.'
Or as:
'The gentle wind of the <s>Kāverī</s> riverbanks, shaking the sandalwood trees, scattering the fragrance of <s>kunda</s> blooms,

makes the <s>Lāṭī</s> woman dance on her forehead, with disheveled locks, [her garland] of flowers fallen from [her lover's] playful tugging, [fragrant] down to the roots of the straight <s>sarala</s> trees.'
Thus other continuations [of seasonal signs] as well.
'The continuations of <s>vicakila</s>, <s>kerasara</s>, <s>pāṭalī</s>, and <s>campa</s> flowers belong to summer.
And therein, some wish for <s>marubaka</s> also, [even though it is] a product of the cold season.'
As [illustrated by]:

children.text: "karṇe smeraṃ śirīṣaṃ śirasi vicakilasraglatāḥ pāṭalinyaḥ kaṇṭhe mārṇālahāro valayitamasitābhbhojanālaṃ kalācyoḥ /
children.translated_text: 'A smiling <s>śirīṣa</s> flower at the ear, garlands of <s>vicakila</s> creepers on the head, a lotus-stalk necklace at the throat, a dark lotus-stem bracelet at the wrists,

children.text: samodaṃ candanābhbhaḥ stanabhuvi nayane mlānanāñjiṣṭhapṛṣṭhe gātraṃ lolajjalārdraṃ jayati mṛgadṛśāṃ grauṣmiko veṣa eṣaḥ" //
children.translated_text: fragrant sandalwood paste on the breasts, eyes with the back [lined with] fading <s>nāñjiṣṭha</s>, the body glistening and moist with water — victorious is this summer attire of doe-eyed women!'
And as:
'A <s>śirīṣa</s> at the ear, rivaling the needle of fresh <s>kuśa</s> grass; a garland of <s>pāṭalā</s> surrounded by <s>marubaka</s> at the throat;

children.text: sa tu sarasajalārdenmīlitaḥ sundarīṇāṃ dinapariṇatijanmā ko 'pi veṣaścakāsti" //
children.translated_text: that certain indescribable attire of beautiful women, born at the turn of day, moist and blooming with fresh water, shines forth.'
Thus other examples [may be supplied].
'The seasonal occurrences and continuations have been indicated here only in outline by the learned;
see the rest with your own intellect — how much can we say by naming [everything]?
In different regions, a reversal of the natural form of objects is observed;
that should not be so bound — what poets have composed is our authority here.'
A flower is useful in six ways: through beauty, fragrance, garlands, offerings, and fruit.
These six have been shown — the seventh is non-use.
As [illustrated by]:

children.text: yatprāci māse kusumaṃ nibaddhaṃ taduttare bālaphalaṃ vidheyam /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever flower is bound in the first month — in the next, its young fruit should be depicted;

children.text: tadagrime prauḍhidharaṃ ca kāryaṃ tadagrime pākapariṣkṛtaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: in the one after that, it should be made to bear mature fruit; and in the one after that, fruit perfected by ripening.'

children.text: drumodbhavānāṃ vidhireṣu dṛṣṭo ballīphalānā na mahānanehā /
children.translated_text: 'This rule is observed for tree-born [fruits]; for creeper-fruits, not much deviation from this.

children.text: teṣāṃ dvimāsāvadhireva kāryaḥ paṣpe phale pākavidhau ca kālaḥ //
children.translated_text: For them, a period of two months should be assigned — for flower, fruit, and the process of ripening.'
'Internal-sheathed, external-sheathed, external-and-internal-sheathed,

children.text: sarvavyājaṃ bahuvyājaṃ nirvyājaṃ ca tathā phalam //
children.translated_text: all-sheathed, many-sheathed, and unsheathed — thus are fruits [classified].'
'<s>Lakuca</s> (breadfruit) and the like are internal-sheathed; <s>mocā</s> (banana) and the like are external-sheathed;
mango and the like are both-sheathed; <s>kakubha</s> (Arjuna tree) and the like are all-sheathed.'
'<s>Panasa</s> (jackfruit) and the like are many-sheathed; <s>nīlakapittha</s> (wood-apple) and the like are unsheathed.
This sixfold classification of all fruits should be known by poets.'
'The seasons should be composed in literary works with the distinction of one, two, three, and so on, or collectively,
in sequence or out of sequence.'
'And there is no fault of disorder for a poet who touches the path of meaning;

children.text: tathā tathā kāpi bhaved vyutkramo bhūṣāṇāṃ yathā //
children.translated_text: just as some [manner of] disorder of ornaments [can itself become beautiful].'
'For one devoid of careful observation, an ornament becomes a blemish;
but for a careful poet, even a blemish becomes an ornament.'
'Thus has been shown this kind of practice regarding the division of time;
herein, a poet [may fall into] great delusion — [but] herein [also] a great poet is proven.'

body.text: iti rājaśekharakṛtau kāvyamīmāṃsāyāṃ kavirahasye prathame 'dhikaraṇe kālavibhāgo nāma aṣṭādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus in the work composed by <s>Rājaśekhara</s>, in the <s>Kāvyamīmāṃsā</s>, in the <s>Kavirahasya</s>, in the first section — the eighteenth chapter, named <s>Kālavibhāga</s> (Division of Time), ends.

body.text: samātpamidaṃ prathamamadhikaraṇaṃ kavirahasyaṃ kāvyamīmāṃsāyām
body.translated_text: Thus is completed the first section, the <s>Kavirahasya</s> (Poet's Secret), in the <s>Kāvyamīmāṃsā</s>.
